conventions.frequency_class: swing = daily-to-weekly trade frequency (core); slow = weekly/monthly published systems, use as overlays; calendar = known-date events only.
conventions.status: active = implement; demoted = control/falsification/overlay only; dropped = documented null, excluded from the queue; forward_test_only = cannot be backtested cleanly, live paper capture only.
conventions.execution: Signals from completed session t; entries at open of t+1 unless the rule names the close. Close-based systems use three fill models: moc_proxy (primary), next_open, close (upper bound only). Open-based signals fill at the 09:31 bar close, never at the signal open. Exits on completed data execute next open unless a close is named. Overnight-only systems enter at the close using information through t-1 (or the 15:50 bar). Stops: long stop fills min(open, stop), short stop/buy-stop max(open, level); stop-entry orders fill max(open, level) / min(open, level); same-bar stop and target -> stop first. Announcement exits include the reaction. Where an entry lists alternatives, the FIRST-listed is the primary baseline.
conventions.costs: Cost ladder: 0.5/1/2/5 bps per side for SPY overnight/auction fills (report break-even cost); 5 bps liquid ETFs; stocks spread/ADV-aware (2-4 bps top dollar-volume decile, 20-60 bps small caps; catalog default 10-15 bps); turnover table required; shorts long-only first with borrow scenarios (0.3%/3%/10%). Reconcile with repo constants (10 bps commission + 15 bps slippage).
conventions.data: Two series per symbol: tr (total return) and raw (unadjusted OHLC + dividends at ex-date); PIT universes by the liquid_top_N rule (top N by 60-day median dollar volume, price >= 5, >= 250 bars; N=500/1500/100); delisted names included, delisting return -30% performance / 0% cash merger; maximum available history plus 1 year warm-up (stock cache starts 2016-01-04); regime-coverage table 2016-19, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023-26.
conventions.validation: Trial registry per (strategy, variant, parameters); Deflated Sharpe > 0.95 on test; dev 2016-01..2023-12, test 2024-01+ locked; AGENTS.md partition table required for dev and test; min 100 independent trades (or 8 years monthly) in dev and 30 in test else 'insufficient evidence'; class baselines (exposure-matched timing, unconditional overnight drift, vol-matched equal-weight, equal-weight rotation universe, hedge-ratio-shuffled pairs, placebo dates); class gates replace Sharpe>2/PF>2 (rotation: baseline+0.2 Sharpe, DSR>0.9; swing: net PF>=1.3 and expectancy >= 2x round-trip cost); one champion per correlation cluster; earnings-window flag for single-stock mean reversion; research scale and paper scale ($5,000, 5 positions) reported separately.
conventions.llm_news_warning: S056, S057 (forward test only), S058, S060 require timestamped news archives and frozen models; current LLMs applied to old news carry look-ahead risk. The repo news archive is ~75k rows from 2023-09. S052/S086 are earnings-calendar strategies, not LLM/news.

strategies.name: RSI(2) Classic (Connors) - cluster control (absorbs S002, S092)
strategies.concept: Deep short-term oversold readings inside a bull regime revert to the mean within days; Connors found buying RSI(2) below 5 returned more than below 10.
strategies.universe: SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA plus the 11 SPDR sector ETFs (per-ETF and pooled results)
strategies.indicators: RSI(2) on closes; SMA(200); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: Gate AND RSI(2)(t) < 10; buy at close of t. Gate: Close(t) > SMA200 (primary). fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound. Position size: one full unit (primary).
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session (primary). No stop in the primary; disaster-stop variant: close < entry - 3 x ATR(14).
strategies.frequency: several trades per month on SPY
strategies.notes: StockCharts: SMA200 filter, RSI(2) < 10 (below 5 returned more), exit above 5-day SMA, buy before the close, no stops. Independent evidence says the edge is regime-limited and post-2000 (Trading Garden S&P 500: 1963-today CAGR 5.4% vs 10.9% buy-and-hold; 2000-today 8.6% vs 8.3%, 187 trades; Be The Puck: beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 50/371 stocks). Cluster control for the whole Connors family (S003-S014, S030); report per-ETF and pooled, vs exposure-matched random timing and vs buy-and-hold / SMA200 timing. Merged strategies: S002 (sizing) and S092 (alternative regime gate) are parameters of this entry; every combination below is a registered trial.
strategies.parameter_variants: RSI threshold {10 primary, 5}; exit {close > SMA5 primary, RSI(2) > 70}; fill {moc_proxy primary, next_open, close}; gate {SMA200 primary, 21-day return > 0 (ex-S092: replaces the 200-day gate, faster regime adaptation)}; sizing {single unit primary, pyramid3 (ex-S002: unit = 1/3 of the position budget; buy 1 unit at RSI(2) < 10, add 1 unit on each NEW session with RSI(2) < 5 while holding, max 3 units, all units exit together on close > SMA5)}; disaster stop {off primary, close < entry - 3 x ATR(14)}

strategies.name: RSI(4) 25/75 (Connors)
strategies.concept: Slightly slower RSI smooths the oversold signal; Connors' original used exit at RSI 75, but the modified exit at 55 halves drawdowns with similar expectancy.
strategies.indicators: RSI(4); SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Close(t) > SMA200 AND RSI(4)(t) < 25; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: RSI(4) > 55; sell at close of that session (primary). Registered alternate: RSI(4) > 75 (Connors' original).
strategies.notes: Quantified Strategies reports QQQ profit factor 2.5, 76% win, 148 trades (~7 trades/yr), 0.9% avg gain; the same page's table shows PF 2.97 (inception to Nov-2020), so the page is internally inconsistent - retest and report a bootstrap CI for PF. The exit level 55 was chosen with hindsight from drawdown results (a selected parameter): count 55 and 75 as separate trials. The 'add a second unit if RSI(4) < 20' variant is NOT part of the baseline. Same trigger family as S001 (G-10).
strategies.parameter_variants: exit {RSI(4) > 55 primary, RSI(4) > 75}; fill {moc_proxy, next_open}

strategies.name: Cumulative RSI(2)
strategies.concept: Summing RSI(2) over 2 days measures sustained capitulation rather than a single extreme print, filtering out one-day spikes.
strategies.universe: liquid stocks (price > $5, 21-day avg volume > 500k, liquid_top_N) and, as a SEPARATE study, liquid ETFs; never pooled
strategies.indicators: Cumulative RSI = RSI(2)(t) + RSI(2)(t-1); SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Close > SMA200 AND cumulative RSI(2,2) = RSI(2)(t) + RSI(2)(t-1) < 35; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: RSI(2) > 65; sell at close of that session (Connors' original, primary)
strategies.sources: [DYR - Cumulative RSI strategy](https://tradingwithdyr.com/cumulative-rsi-strategy/) (page could not be retrieved in review; verify); Connors/Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work, chapter on cumulative RSI (rule as transcribed: cumulative RSI(2,2) below 35 above SMA200, exit RSI(2) > 65); Quantitativo replication (blog claim, unverified)
strategies.notes: Primary now follows Connors' original (thresholds 35 / 65), not the earlier threshold-20 selection with an up-close next-open exit. Registered alternates: threshold 20 with exit close > SMA5; threshold 10 with exit at next open (Quantitativo, 3 positions, large caps, ~26%/yr blog claim). Trading Garden S&P 500 (cumulative RSI): 1963-today CAGR 8.3%; 2000-today 10.6% (199 trades). Single-stock runs are earnings-window contaminated: report with and without signals within +/-3 sessions of an earnings release (G-12).
strategies.parameter_variants: threshold/exit {cum RSI(2,2) < 35 & RSI(2) > 65 primary; cum RSI < 20 & close > SMA5 or first up-close; cum RSI < 10 & exit at next open (Quantitativo)}; tested thresholds 2/5/10/15/20/35; fill {moc_proxy, next_open}
strategies.data_needs: stocks: daily_10years (D1) + earnings flag (DP-EARN); ETFs: DP-ETF total-return

strategies.name: Connors %b (Bollinger Band)
strategies.concept: %b < 0.2 for three consecutive days is a persistent stretch below the lower Bollinger Band. With BB(20,2) this is a genuinely rare state; with the 5-day band Quantified Strategies uses, it is close to 'three down days' (a 5-bar band is dominated by the last three closes). They are different strategies sharing a name, so both are registered.
strategies.universe: primary: Connors' ETF list (e.g., DIA, EEM, EFA, EWH, EWJ, EWT, EWZ, FXI, GLD, ILF, IWM, IYR, QQQ, SPY, XHB, XLB, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLV; use those with data); secondary: SPY/QQQ single-position version
strategies.indicators: Bollinger %b, BB(20,2) with POPULATION std (ddof=0) primary; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Close > SMA200 AND %b < 0.2 for 3 consecutive sessions; buy at close of the third session (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: %b > 0.8; sell at close of that session
strategies.frequency: several trades per month per ETF
strategies.notes: Connors did not publish the lookback. Primary BB(20,2) matches the book as transcribed (a StockFetcher transcription quotes Connors' ETF results: 1,014 trades, 76.5% win, +0.70%/trade, 4.2-day hold; the same poster reports every trade since 4/16/2010 negative in a later test). QS variant: 5-day lookback, 2 sd. Be The Puck %b beats buy-and-hold Sharpe on only 19% of 371 stocks (invested ~18% of days, worst on big tech). Run the single-position SPY/QQQ version and the multi-ETF portfolio as two separate studies.
strategies.parameter_variants: band {BB(20,2) primary, BB(5,2) (Quantified Strategies)}; universe {Connors ETF list, SPY/QQQ only}

strategies.name: Double 7s
strategies.concept: A 7-day closing low in a bull regime is a statistically favorable dip: no stop loss, exit at the opposite 7-day extreme, letting mean reversion complete.
strategies.universe: SPY or broad ETFs, pooled across ETFs (SPY alone gives ~5 trades/yr, ~50 in a 10-year window)
strategies.indicators: 7-day rolling low of closes; 7-day rolling high of closes; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Close(t) > SMA200 AND close(t) <= the lowest close of the last 7 sessions INCLUDING session t (inclusive window, ties count as a low); buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close >= the highest close of the last 7 sessions including session t; sell at close of that session. No stop in the primary; disaster-stop variant: close < entry x (1 - 3 x ATR%).
strategies.frequency: ~1-2 trades per month on SPY (154 trades since 1993 per Quantified Strategies)
strategies.notes: Best-evidenced Connors rule but regime-dependent: Trading Garden S&P 500: 252 trades since 2000, 76% win, CAGR 11.9% vs 8.3% buy-and-hold, but 1963-today 7.5% with a 33-year longest drawdown; Be The Puck beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 86/371. Quantified Strategies SPY since 1993: 154 trades; lookback robust from 2 to 15 days. Report the full lookback surface (not the best cell). Window definition must be inclusive with <= / >= ties because libraries differ.
strategies.parameter_variants: lookback {7 primary, 5, 10} (report the whole surface); disaster stop {off primary, close < entry x (1 - 3 x ATR%)}; fill {moc_proxy, next_open}
strategies.review: KEEP (cluster champion candidate) | source OK (rule); QS page unfetchable

strategies.name: 3-Day Pullback
strategies.concept: Three consecutive lower closes inside an uptrend exhaust short-term sellers; exit when the 5-day mean is recovered.
strategies.indicators: 3-day close streak; SMA(200); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: Close > SMA200 AND three consecutive sessions with close < prior close; buy at close of the third session (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session
strategies.sources: Connors/Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (multiple-days-down chapter); [CXO Advisory - book review (principles only, no rule or numbers)](https://www.cxoadvisory.com/technical-trading/a-few-notes-on-short-term-trading-strategies-that-work/)
strategies.notes: The CXO page is a book review: Connors' general principles (buy pullbacks, above the 200-day, buy fear, no stops, hold overnight) and a warning that the analyses are 'hypothetical backtests without transaction costs or data mining corrections' (1995-2007). It contains NO 'three lower closes, exit above 5-day SMA' rule and no performance numbers. The rule is plausible but unsourced here. Same trigger family as S001/S009/S030: run it as the N=3 member of the down-streak family (N = 2..7) together with S030.
strategies.parameter_variants: streak length N {3 primary; 2..7 as the family grid shared with S009 and S030}

strategies.name: ConnorsRSI(3,2,100) Stock Pullback
strategies.concept: Buys strong trending stocks (ADX > 30) after a sharp one-day capitulation (ConnorsRSI < 10 with close in bottom 25% of day range), selling on recovery to ConnorsRSI > 70.
strategies.universe: liquid US stocks (guidebook: price > $5, volume > 250k, 200-day history)
strategies.indicators: ConnorsRSI(3,2,100) = (RSI(close,3) + RSI(streak,2) + PercentRank(ROC(1),100))/3 with Wilder smoothing, streak = signed count of consecutive up/down closes, PercentRank over the prior 100 one-day returns; ADX(10); gap-from-close and close-location filters (this entry exceeds the old 4-indicator cap; the cap is dropped, see shared spec)
strategies.entry: ADX(10) > 30 AND low(t) at least 4% below prior close AND close in bottom 25% of day range AND ConnorsRSI < 10; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound). Alternate: guidebook limit order at next session, 2-10% below signal close, filled only if low(t+1) <= limit (report the fill rate)
strategies.exit: ConnorsRSI > 70; sell at close of that session
strategies.notes: Be The Puck matches (ADX(10) > 30, low >= 4% below prior close, close in bottom 25% of the range, CRSI < 10, exit CRSI > 70; $5 / 250k-volume filters; no 200-day filter) but its scorecard is the weakest of the Connors rules: calls right 59% over 8,172 calls, beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on only 42/371. The guidebook's primary fill is the next-day limit 2-10% below the close; a limit fill creates adverse selection (you fill precisely on continuation days), so backtest both with fill-probability reported. A 4% intraday drop with a bottom-quartile close is largely earnings/news: report with and without earnings-window signals (+/-3 sessions, G-12).
strategies.parameter_variants: fill {signal-close (moc_proxy) primary, next_open, guidebook limit 2% / 5% / 10% below close}; earnings-window {included, excluded}

strategies.name: 3 Days Down Overnight (SPY)
strategies.concept: The overnight session (close-to-open) captures most of the mean reversion after multi-day selloffs; holding only overnight avoids giving back the bounce intraday.
strategies.indicators: 3-day down-close streak
strategies.entry: SPY closes lower for 3 consecutive sessions; buy at close of the third session (moc_proxy; next_open not applicable to the overnight version)
strategies.exit: Sell at next day's open (overnight capture, primary); next day's close (full-day version, alternate)
strategies.frequency: ~4-8 trades per year on SPY (pool QQQ, IWM, DIA and sector ETFs to raise the count)
strategies.notes: The Quantified Strategies Substack post is paywalled: only the rule sentence is visible (three consecutive down days, SPY since 1993, Amibroker). The earlier '212 trades' figure belonged to the Turnaround Tuesday statistic (S010) and is removed; trade count and performance for THIS rule are unverified. The relevant null is the unconditional close-to-open return of SPY (see S021), which is itself positive: report conditional minus unconditional overnight difference using the dividend-correct overnight series (raw open/close plus dividends at the ex-date), with a placebo of 2- and 4-day streaks.
strategies.parameter_variants: streak length {3 primary; placebo 2 and 4}; exit {next open primary, next close}; universe {SPY, then pooled QQQ/IWM/DIA/sector ETFs}

strategies.name: Turnaround Tuesday (absorbs S085)
strategies.concept: A weak Monday tends to reverse on Tuesday. The relevant nulls are the unconditional Tuesday and unconditional post-down-day drift; calendar effects are the weakest evidence class (Atlas 9.5) and Be The Puck notes the Monday effect 'vanished after 1975'.
strategies.indicators: Monday close-to-close return; weekday filter; optional VIX day-over-day change
strategies.entry: On Monday, if close(Mon) < close(Fri) (primary, Monday close-to-close weakness), buy at Monday close
strategies.exit: Sell at Tuesday open (overnight, primary); Tuesday close (alternate)
strategies.sources: [Papers With Backtest - Turnaround Tuesday (generic article; its two code snippets define 'Monday drop' inconsistently and one computes win ratio by conditioning on the outcome, i.e. look-ahead)](https://paperswithbacktest.com/course/turnaround-tuesday)
strategies.notes: Earlier note corrected: the 56% win rate, 212 trades and 0.3% avg gain are Quantified Strategies figures (unverified) and do not appear on the cited page. The old rule 'open(t) < close(t-1)' was a Monday GAP-down, a different event from a weak Monday; both are now explicit variants. Run the identical rule for every weekday as a placebo. Absorbs S085 (enhanced variant).
strategies.parameter_variants: Monday weakness {close(Mon) < close(Fri) primary; return <= -0.5% (ex-S085: Monday close-to-close decline > 0.5%); gap-down open(Mon) < close(Fri)}; VIX filter {off primary; VIX(t) > VIX(t-1) (ex-S085)}; exit {Tuesday open, Tuesday close}; placebo weekdays {Mon..Fri}
strategies.data_needs: ETF raw prices (DP-ETF); VIX for the S085 filter (DP-VIX)

strategies.name: Z-Score / Bollinger Lower-Band Mean Reversion (absorbs S012)
strategies.concept: A close more than 2 standard deviations below its 20-day mean (z < -2, algebraically identical to a close below the lower Bollinger Band(20,2) up to ddof) is a >95th-percentile stretch; the 20-day mean is the magnet. S011 (z-score with SMA200 gate) and S012 (lower-band close with RSI(2) filter, no gate) are cells of one family.
strategies.indicators: z = (close - SMA20)/std20 of closes (population std, ddof=0) or equivalently Bollinger Bands(20,2); SMA(200) gate (optional); RSI(2) filter (optional)
strategies.entry: z(t) < -2 (close below BB(20,2) lower band) AND Close > SMA200; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: z(t) > 0 (close above the 20-day middle band); sell at close of that session
strategies.sources: [Quantified Strategies - 200 free backtested strategies (index page, no rule)](https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/trading-strategies-free/); Be The Puck Bollinger Reversion scorecard (cross-check)
strategies.notes: Be The Puck's Bollinger Reversion (close below the lower band, exit at the 20-day mean) beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 56/372 and returned 5.7%/yr vs 8.9% buy-and-hold on the S&P 500 index: weak as a standalone. The ex-S012 form has no SMA200 gate, which makes it a bear-market catcher; the gate is therefore a registered switch. State ddof=0 (pandas default std is ddof=1). Report the four cells as ONE cluster result.
strategies.parameter_variants: SMA200 gate {on primary, off (ex-S012)} x RSI(2) < 10 filter {off primary, on (ex-S012)} (four trials); universe {SPY, QQQ, IWM}; ddof {0 primary, 1}

strategies.name: TLT Mean Reversion (RSI(2))
strategies.concept: Long Treasuries are among the most mean-reverting daily assets (safe-haven flows reverse); Connors-style RSI(2) rules transfer to TLT.
strategies.indicators: RSI(2); SMA(200); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: Close > SMA200 AND RSI(2) < 10; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session
strategies.notes: Connors' rules applied to TLT (application is the catalog's). IndicatorEdge's TLT backtests found few daily setups beating buy-and-hold: the edge must be confirmed, not assumed. TLT/SHY must be total-return series (distributions are most of the return) and results must be split by rate regime (2016-19, 2020, 2022 when TLT sat below its SMA200 most of the year so the filter removes trades).

strategies.name: Sector ETF Basket Mean Reversion
strategies.concept: Buying the 3 weakest sector ETFs of the past 5 sessions (while above their 200-day SMA) diversifies single-ETF timing risk and harvests cross-sector reversal.
strategies.universe: SPDR sector ETFs defined by a PIT inception-date table (9 sectors until XLRE Oct-2015 and XLC Jun-2018; XLK/XLY/XLC reconstituted Sep-2018, which breaks price continuity - note the break); the same table is used by S042
strategies.indicators: 5-day return minus beta x SPY 5-day return (60-day beta through t-1); raw 5-day return (variant); SMA(200); SMA(5) or SMA(10)
strategies.entry: Each session, rank sector ETFs by 5-day residual return vs SPY (primary); buy the 3 worst that have close > SMA200, at the close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary (signal from the 15:50 bar, fill at the official close); next_open alternate; close fill reported only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Per position, close > 5-day SMA (primary, the family convention); sell at close of that session
strategies.sources: [CXO Advisory — Notes on Short Term Trading Strategies That Work](https://www.cxoadvisory.com/technical-trading/a-few-notes-on-short-term-trading-strategies-that-work/)
strategies.notes: Sector ETFs are ~0.8 correlated, so a raw '5-day worst 3 of 9' mostly ranks beta to the day's market move; ranking on the residual vs SPY ties to S075. The CXO page has no basket rule. The earlier 10-day SMA exit differed from the family without justification and is now a registered alternate.
strategies.parameter_variants: rank {residual vs SPY primary, raw 5-day return}; exit {SMA5 primary, SMA10}
strategies.data_needs: sector ETF total-return daily series (DP-ETF) + PIT sector universe table

strategies.name: Chan Buy-on-Gap (absorbs S022)
strategies.concept: Panic gap-down opens in stocks still in uptrends (open above 20-day MA) are overreactions; buying the open and exiting at the same day's close harvests intraday recovery. This is Chan's documented strategy from Quantitative Trading.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks (N=1500, SP1500-like, PIT price-only rule)
strategies.indicators: 90-day POPULATION std of close-to-close returns; 20-day SMA
strategies.entry: Signal from the open: select stocks where return from prior day's low to today's open < -1 std (std on prior 90 days of close-to-close returns, ddof=0); keep only those with open > 20-day SMA of closes; buy the 10 deepest qualifying drops. Fill: the close of the 09:31 bar (first-minute bar after the signal) with 15 bps RTH slippage (a signal computed from open(t) cannot be filled at open(t))
strategies.exit: Sell all positions at the SAME session's close (Chan's published form, primary); next session's open is the registered alternate
strategies.frequency: ~0.5 qualifying positions per day on average (the reproduction took 695 positions in 1,500 days, held at least one name on 391 days and the full ten on only ten days)
strategies.notes: l3a0 reproduces Chan's printed APR 8.7% / Sharpe 1.5 on his own survivor-biased file (497 stocks, 2006-05 to 2012-04, no costs; with the other std helper 8.4%/1.7). Chan traded a version that 'suffered from diminishing returns from 2009 onward' and a trader cannot know the official open in time (pre-open quotes pick different stocks). Our 2016+ sample is entirely post-decay: run as a pre-registered falsification test with an expected skill of about zero. Absorbs S022 (fixed-percentage trigger).
strategies.parameter_variants: gap rule {Chan std-based primary; fixed_pct (ex-S022): open(t)/close(t-1) - 1 < -1% / -2% / -3% AND close(t-1) > SMA200 (S022 used a fixed -2%, S&P 500 stocks, which fires in bulk in March 2020 and 2022)}; exit {same-day close primary, next open}; std {population primary, sample}
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + 09:31 minute bars for candidate days

strategies.name: Short-on-Gap-Up (Chan mirror)
strategies.concept: The mirror of Chan's buy-on-gap: stocks that gap up more than 1 std against a downtrend revert intraday.
strategies.indicators: 90-day std of close-to-close returns; 20-day SMA
strategies.entry: Signal from the open: select stocks where return from prior day's high to today's open > +1 std (ddof=0); keep only those with open < 20-day SMA; short the 10 largest qualifying gap-ups. Fill at the close of the 09:31 bar with 15 bps slippage
strategies.exit: Cover at the SAME session's close (Chan's published form, primary); next session's open alternate
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the l3a0 reproduction found the declared mirror rule PROFITABLE pre-cost (APR 12.2%, Sharpe 1.79, 725 shorts, survivor-biased, no costs) versus Chan's published 46% / 1.27; what failed was the match to Chan's published figure (a volatility-floor argument shows whatever Chan ran moved >= 4.5x as much as the declared rule). The steeper drawdown claim does reproduce (-6.5% vs -5.2%). Same fill issues, borrow/recall risk and survivorship as S015. Test as the hedge leg of S015 (market-neutral basket) under borrow scenarios (0.3% GC, 3%, 10% annualised); run long-only first for the rest of the catalog.

strategies.name: Night Trading Overnight-Bias Stock Selection (absorbs S034)
strategies.concept: Roughly one-fifth of stocks have persistent, statistically significant positive overnight-return biases; holding only their overnight sessions earned twice the market's return with one-third the beta (SSRN). These stocks tend to have negative intraday returns — the premium is paid for overnight risk-bearing.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks with 1+ year of history (liquidity floor, price >= $5)
strategies.indicators: trailing 252-day mean overnight return (close-to-open, from raw prices plus dividends added back at the ex-date) and its t-statistic; unconditional overnight drift of the same stocks as null
strategies.entry: Formation: each year (primary) compute each stock's trailing-252-day mean overnight return and t-stat; select stocks with t > 2 (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-controlled) AND in the top quintile of mean overnight return. Evaluation: hold the selected set through the NEXT calendar year (formation year selects, next year evaluates; do not roll the screen daily). Each day buy at the close (auction/MOC fill)
strategies.exit: Sell at next open (MOO fill); repeat daily (pure overnight capture)
strategies.sources: [SSRN — Night Trading: Lower Risk But Higher Returns?](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2633476)
strategies.notes: Lachance (SSRN 2633476; single author, also Rev. Financial Economics): one fifth of stocks have significant positive overnight biases; investing overnight in them the next year yields twice the market return for a third of the beta, and they average negative returns intraday. The t > 2 screen is the catalog's operationalisation (about 2.3% pass by chance one-sided vs 20% flagged, hence FDR). A daily round trip costs 2 x (half-spread + slippage): at 10-15 bps per side that is 25-38%/yr, comparable to the claimed premium: use auction fills and report the break-even cost. Opening-print bid-ask bounce biases measured overnight returns upward (use first-minute VWAP/mid for exits where minute data exist, plus a liquidity floor). Add Lou-Polk-Skouras (2019 JFE, 'A tug of war', verify citation) persistence as a robustness check. Absorbs S034: the cross-sectional monthly-formation variant and its holding conventions below.
strategies.parameter_variants: formation cadence {annual primary; quarterly; monthly (ex-S034)}; holding convention {overnight-only primary; full-day; long overnight / short intraday of the same stocks}; extra filter {none primary; negative trailing intraday return (ex-S034, kept only if it improves a hold-out)}; hold {daily overnight primary; one week dropped}
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years raw OHLC (D1) + dividend calendar (DP-CAL) for dividend-correct overnight returns

strategies.name: Gap Fade (Fill the Gap)
strategies.concept: Common gaps (not driven by material news) tend to fill — price returns to the prior close — as overnight overreaction unwinds.
strategies.indicators: gap size vs 20-day average true range; volume filter (gap on below-average volume = common gap)
strategies.entry: Step 1 (descriptive study, before any simulation): measure P(fill by close | gap bucket) and P(fill within 3 sessions) by gap size x trend x catalyst flag. Step 2 (rule): 0.5 x ATR(20) <= |gap| < 1.0 x ATR(20) (band disjoint from S019's > 1 ATR) AND no earnings/FOMC/dividend catalyst in the calendar AND prior-5-session average volume below its 20-day average (quiet-tape proxy, a property of the prior tape not of the gap); buy down-gaps / short up-gaps; fill at the close of the 09:31 bar
strategies.exit: Same-day close (primary); next open and the gap-fill target (prior close) are registered alternates
strategies.notes: Capital.com is a qualitative education page (common/breakaway/runaway/exhaustion gaps), no numbers. The gap-fill thesis is an intraday/few-day statement, hence the same-day-close primary. Gap-day volume is unknown at the open, so 'common vs breakaway' cannot be resolved; the quiet-tape proxy is the catalog's. Catalysts: earnings from SimFin Publish Date (2009+) / EDGAR 8-K 2.02 (2023-09+); FOMC and dividend calendars must be built. Report expected signal frequency per 500 stocks before sizing the trial. S018 and S019 partition gap-size/volume space so the two never trade the same name in opposite directions.
strategies.parameter_variants: exit {same-day close primary, next open, gap-fill target}; gap band {0.5-1.0 ATR primary}; catalyst filter {on}
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + 09:31 minute bars + earnings/FOMC/dividend calendars (DP-EARN, DP-CAL)

strategies.name: Gap-and-Go Continuation (absorbs S025)
strategies.concept: Breakaway gaps with high volume tend to continue in the gap direction — institutional repositioning does not complete in one session.
strategies.universe: liquid stocks (primary); index ETFs SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA and sector ETFs (ex-S025 index version, same code, different universe)
strategies.indicators: gap size vs ATR(20); relative volume (gap-session volume vs 20-day median); R defined below
strategies.entry: Open(t) > close(t-1) by more than 1 x ATR(20) AND volume by end of session > 2 x 20-day median; buy at close of t (confirmed breakaway). Mirror short for down-gaps (long-only first)
strategies.exit: Stop = prior close (primary; alternate: gap-day low), so R = entry - stop; target 2R or trail at 2-bar low; max hold 5 sessions
strategies.notes: Capital.com's gap-and-go: high-volume gap, enter in gap direction, stop just inside the gap area, 1:2 or 1:3 reward-to-risk on intraday charts; adapted here to daily bars with close confirmation. With a close entry after a >1 ATR gap the stop 'just inside the gap' is the prior close, i.e. >1 ATR away, and a 1:2 target is >2 ATR: hence explicit R. The Atlas (10.4, Mittal & Choudhary 2026) argues quiet-looking moves travel further than visually impressive breakouts, the opposite of the 2x-volume rule: both volume regimes are registered. Index version (ex-S025): open(t) > high(t-1) AND session volume > 1.5 x 20-day median, buy at close, exit close of t+2 or trail 2-bar low, max 3 sessions; SPY alone gives only ~15-25 events a decade, so pool the ETF set; test both signs (long continuation / short fade) as registered variants only if costs allow.
strategies.parameter_variants: volume regime {> 2x median primary, < 1x median}; stop {prior close primary, gap-day low}; universe {stocks, index/sector ETFs (ex-S025: open > prior high, volume > 1.5x median, exit close t+2 / 2-bar low, max 3 sessions)}; direction on indices {long continuation primary; short fade}

strategies.name: Earnings-Eve Estimate-Drift Mean Reversion (Chan/Estimize)
strategies.concept: Chan's documented price-only benchmark: stocks whose return over the full estimate period exceeds the return over the recent (latest-20%) estimate period — delta = R − Rs > 0 — are the ones to BUY into the announcement; the overnight session after the announcement captures the drift.
strategies.universe: US stocks with quarterly earnings the next session
strategies.indicators: delta = R (return over average estimate-reporting period T) − Rs (return over the latest 20% of the estimate period); earnings calendar
strategies.entry: On the close before an earnings announcement: buy stocks with delta > 0 (full-period return exceeds recent-period return); short stocks with delta < 0
strategies.exit: Exit at the open after the announcement (overnight capture of the earnings reaction)
strategies.sources: [Ernest Chan — Trading with Estimize and I/B/E/S earnings estimates](http://epchan.blogspot.com/2015/01/trading-with-estimize-and-ibes-earnings.html)
strategies.notes: DOCUMENTED NULL, dropped from the active queue. In the source post (guest author Yang Gao, QTS Capital) the price-only delta rule is a BENCHMARK to show Estimize data carries information: 'This benchmark shows no significant positive return'. The strategies that earned returns were Deltix's Estimize mean-reversion (S&P 100, 2012-2013, Sharpe 0.8, 6%/yr after 5 bps) and an I/B/E/S momentum rule (Sharpe 1.5, 11%) that failed out of sample (2010-2011: -6.4%); the authors conclude 'we cannot have a statistically significant backtest'. The post also hedges net exposure with SPY, which this entry omits, and delta needs estimate-reporting dates a price-only run cannot define. If ever run: falsification test only (expect null) with an SPY hedge.
strategies.data_needs: BLOCKED for the profitable variant (Estimize/IBES estimates not available); price-only version is a null control

strategies.name: Index Overnight Premium (SPY close-to-open only; absorbs S084)
strategies.concept: Nearly all of SPY's long-term return accrues overnight; holding only the overnight session captures the premium with lower volatility than full-day holding.
strategies.indicators: SMA(50) participation filter (optional, registered trial); dividend-correct overnight return = (raw open(t+1) + dividend if ex-date)/raw close(t) - 1
strategies.entry: Buy SPY at every close (unconditional, primary); filtered variant: only when close(t) > SMA(50)
strategies.exit: Sell at every open (cash intraday)
strategies.sources: [SSRN - Night Trading: Lower Risk But Higher Returns? (stock-selection evidence; see S017)](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2633476); Cooper, Cliff & Gulen, Return Differences between Trading and Non-trading Hours (SSRN 1004081): the US equity premium over their decade is solely due to overnight returns for stocks, indexes and index futures
strategies.notes: Market-level evidence is Cooper-Cliff-Gulen, not Lachance (stock selection); the SMA(50) filter is the catalog's adaptation. At 5 bps/side the strategy loses by arithmetic (504 sides a year = 25%/yr): the result is purely a function of the cost assumption, so run a cost-sensitivity ladder (0.5 / 1 / 2 / 5 bps per side), report the break-even cost, and use auction fills. A split-only series understates SPY's overnight return by roughly its dividend yield (~1.3-1.5%/yr): use raw open/close plus dividends added back at the ex-date. Null = SPY close-to-open buy-and-hold. Report the per-weekday decomposition and subperiods (2016-19, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023-26) for decay. Absorbs S084 (Friday-close to Monday-open weekend slice): Be The Puck notes the weekend effect 'vanished after 1975', so the weekend slice is a table in this study (test both signs), not a separate strategy.
strategies.parameter_variants: filter {none primary, SMA(50) gate}; cost per side {0.5, 1, 2, 5 bps}; weekday table {Mon..Fri overnight returns, incl. ex-S084 Friday-close to Monday-open, both signs}; universe {SPY primary, QQQ, IWM}

strategies.name: Post-Earnings Overnight Drift
strategies.concept: Earnings surprises that hit pre-market or after-hours create overnight order imbalances that continue into the next open (the overnight portion of PEAD).
strategies.universe: stocks reporting earnings with pre-market/after-hours timing
strategies.indicators: earnings date/surprise sign; overnight gap vs ATR(20)
strategies.entry: Step 1 (descriptive study): open(t) to close(t+1) return by SUE bucket. Step 2 (rule): if earnings are announced outside regular hours (BMO/AMC classified from EDGAR 8-K 2.02 acceptance time, 2023-09+) AND SUE (point-in-time, from SimFin quarterly EPS) is in the top decile on a trailing cutoff AND the gap is < 3 x ATR(20) (not blow-off), buy at the open of the reaction session; misses: short as a separate leg
strategies.exit: Exit at the close of t+1 (one full day plus overnight) or trail 2-bar low
strategies.sources: Earnings Whispers (announcement premium +1.08% for Score +5, NOT post-announcement drift, vendor data): https://www.earningswhispers.com/about-score; Chan's Estimize post is unrelated to PEAD. No direct source for the overnight continuation claim
strategies.notes: The entry buys the open AFTER the surprise gap, so the overnight reaction is already realised; the claimed continuation from open(t) to close(t+1) needs its own evidence. The gap itself must not be used as the surprise. SUE = (EPS_q - EPS_{q-4}) / std of the last 8 such differences (seasonal random walk) at the Publish Date; consensus data is not in the repo. Shorts are a separate later experiment (G-09).
strategies.data_needs: SimFin quarterly EPS + Publish Date; EDGAR 8-K 2.02 timestamps 2023-09+ (DP-EARN); daily_10years (D1)

strategies.name: Ex-Dividend Window Capture (absorbs S101)
strategies.concept: The ex-date price drop is typically 80-100% of the dividend, so gross edge is expected near zero; the study measures the ex-day drop ratio and then P&L over several holding windows. No documented mechanism supports a systematic post-ex recovery.
strategies.universe: liquid high-yield stocks and ETFs; S&P 500 stocks with yield > 2% (~100 names, ~4 ex-dates a year each) for the ex-S101 window
strategies.indicators: ex-dividend calendar; dividend yield vs 20-day price change
strategies.entry: Buy at the close of the session before the ex-dividend date (primary)
strategies.exit: Sell at the open of the ex-date (overnight over the ex-date, primary); alternates: close of the ex-date; close of ex-date +1 (ex-S101: buy close 1 session before ex, sell close 1 session after, 3 sessions)
strategies.sources: [Quantified Strategies - 200 free backtested strategies (index page, no rule)](https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/trading-strategies-free/)
strategies.notes: P&L = ex-date return + dividend; with two spreads, costs and the 61-day qualified-dividend rule the net edge is expected negative for most names. Use UNADJUSTED prices with explicit dividend credits and report the ex-day drop ratio (P_cum_close - P_ex_open)/D by yield bucket before P&L. SimFin 'Dividend' exists only 2020-11 to 2025-10: Alpaca corporate actions or Polygon/Massive are needed for 2016+. Absorbs S101 (hold through the ex-date).
strategies.parameter_variants: hold window {buy close before ex -> sell ex-date open (primary); -> ex-date close; -> ex-date+1 close (ex-S101)}; yield bucket {all; > 2%}

strategies.name: Exhaustion Gap Fade After 3-Day Run
strategies.concept: A stock that gaps up after 3+ consecutive up-closes shows climax behavior; late-stage gaps revert as the last buyers are exhausted.
strategies.indicators: 3-day up-close streak; gap size vs ATR(20); RSI(2)
strategies.entry: 3 consecutive up closes AND open(t) > close(t-1) by more than 1 × ATR(20) AND RSI(2) > 95; short at open of t
strategies.exit: Cover at the open of t+1 (overnight hold — primary); trail 2-bar high alternate; max 3 sessions
strategies.notes: Falsification only. '3 consecutive up closes' already implies a high RSI(2) (the > 95 test is largely redundant); the trade is the opposite side of S019/S100 on similar states; the short is entered at the open on an open-derived signal (fill at the 09:31 bar, G-03.2) with borrow/squeeze risk (G-09). The only source (Capital.com) describes the exhaustion gap as followed by very high volume and appearing near the end of a long trend; this rule has no volume condition and only a 3-day run. No numbers anywhere. Run once as a pre-registered falsification; drop if skill <= 0 at the 5% level with FDR over the gap cluster.

strategies.name: Lehmann 1-Week Loser Reversal
strategies.concept: The classic academic reversal: buy the worst performers over the prior week, hold one week. NY Fed SR 513 (Da, Liu & Schaumburg) decomposes reversal profits into across-industry momentum, within-industry variation in expected returns, under-reaction to within-industry cash-flow news and a residual: only the RESIDUAL ('nonfundamental' price changes) is significant and positive, and a strategy built to capture it earns about 3x the risk-adjusted return of the standard sort (1982-2009, monthly sorts). The best-supported implementation is therefore within-industry (peer-adjusted) reversal, see S075.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks (PIT rule: top N by trailing 60-day median dollar volume, price >= $5, >= 250 prior bars). Research scale: bottom quintile within the top-1000; paper scale ($5,000, 5 positions): top-10 names
strategies.indicators: 5-session trailing return rank; industry-peer and market adjustment (SimFin industries / SIC); optional 1-day skip between formation and holding
strategies.entry: Each week, rank the universe by trailing 5-session return (raw primary; industry-adjusted registered side by side); buy the bottom quintile (research) / worst 10 (paper), equal-weight, at the close of the ranking session (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Hold 5 sessions; rebalance weekly
strategies.frequency: weekly rebalance, always in the market
strategies.sources: [NY Fed Staff Report 513 - Decomposing Short-Term Return Reversal](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr513.html) (monthly sorts, not weekly); Lehmann (1990) weekly reversal; Wu & Jegadeesh (2020): closing-auction impact dissipates over 3-5 days
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the earlier attribution of profits to across-industry momentum and within-industry expected-return variation is wrong (those components are the ones that are NOT significant). Weekly closes carry a bid-ask-bounce component, so report both no-skip and one-day-skip. Weekly turnover is ~100%: at 10 bps/side the drag is ~10%/yr. Long-only beta is ~1.2-1.5 in selloffs, so the null is the vol-matched equal-weight universe with cash. A decile of the top-500 = 50 positions is infeasible at $1,000 per position. Control for S075.
strategies.parameter_variants: adjustment {raw primary, industry-adjusted, industry+market-adjusted}; skip {0 days primary, 1 day}; sort breadth {quintile of top-1000 research, top-10 paper}

strategies.name: Jegadeesh 1-Month Reversal
strategies.concept: Monthly rebalanced reversal: bottom-decile stocks by 1-month return outperform over the next month (Jegadeesh 1990). The NY Fed decomposition (S027) says the monthly strategy works through the within-industry residual, so raw and industry-adjusted versions are both run.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks (PIT price-only rule), price >= $5
strategies.indicators: 21-session trailing return rank
strategies.entry: At each month-end, buy the bottom decile by trailing 21-session return (raw primary; industry-adjusted registered), equal-weight, at the close (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly (hold 1 month)
strategies.sources: Jegadeesh (1990), Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns, J. Finance; [NY Fed Staff Report 513](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr513.html); Be The Puck 1-month reversal scorecard (cross-check)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the attached Borsa Istanbul paper does NOT say reversal is strongest in liquid universes: its literature review says one-month reversal captures microstructure/liquidity effects 'typically strong in thinly traded emerging markets'; its pure reversal portfolio has net Sharpe 0.93 (CAGR 20.0%) vs 1.35 for the 52-week-high anchor and 1.16 for the equal-weight universe, and removing reversal from the blend RAISES net Sharpe by +0.11 (p = 0.12). The paper defines reversal as minus last month's return inside a z-score composite, not a bottom-decile buy. Be The Puck (stock below SPY last month -> hold a month): beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 82/372. Benchmark: vol-matched equal-weight universe. Slower than S027; the monthly member of the reversal family.
strategies.parameter_variants: adjustment {raw primary, industry-adjusted}

strategies.name: Capitulation-Volume Loser Reversal
strategies.concept: Reversal is strongest when the selloff came on extreme volume — panic liquidation (mutual fund redemptions, margin calls) rather than informed selling is most likely to revert.
strategies.indicators: 5-day return rank; volume z-score (20-day); SPY SMA(200) regime (reported both ways); earnings-window flag
strategies.entry: 5-day return in bottom decile AND volume(t) > 3 x 20-day average volume; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound); rank by volume z-score and cap positions per day (the partition account caps at 5). Regime: run with the SPY > SMA200 skip filter AND without it, and report conditional on regime; report with and without signals within +/-3 sessions of an earnings release
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session
strategies.frequency: 2-5 signals per week across the universe
strategies.notes: The regime filter is justified as avoiding falling knives, but the fire-sale mechanism (Coval & Stafford 2005; Atlas 12.5) is concentrated in crashes, so the filter may remove the best events (Mar-2020, Dec-2018). Volume > 3x with a bottom-decile 5-day return is dominated by earnings/news-driven drops: without the earnings flag this is S054/S055 in disguise. Signals fire in clusters on market-wide selloff days, so events are not independent: effective sample size per DAY, cluster-robust standard errors by date.
strategies.parameter_variants: regime filter {SPY > SMA200 on, off}; earnings window {included, excluded}

strategies.name: Down-Streak Reversal (5+ Days)
strategies.concept: Consecutive down days are serially overpredicted by panic sellers; Connors' dip-buying rules show that within uptrends, streaks of down closes are bought profitably.
strategies.indicators: down-close streak count; SMA(200); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: 5+ consecutive down closes AND close > SMA200; buy at close of the 5th down day (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session
strategies.notes: Streaks are the raw material of Connors-style pullback systems; this is the pure streak version without oscillators. Run as the stock-universe member of the down-streak family N = 2..7 together with S007 and S009 (G-10); report with and without signals within +/-3 sessions of an earnings release (G-12). CXO page has general Connors principles only.
strategies.parameter_variants: streak length N {5 primary; 2..7 family grid shared with S007 and S009}; earnings window {included, excluded}

strategies.name: Up-Streak Fade (5+ Days)
strategies.concept: Mirror of S030: extended up-streaks in stocks below their 200-day SMA (weak regime) exhibit short-term exhaustion.
strategies.indicators: up-close streak count; SMA(200); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: 5+ consecutive up closes AND close < SMA200; short at close of the 5th up day
strategies.exit: Close < 5-day SMA OR RSI(2) < 10; cover at close of that session; max 5 sessions
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the earlier note said Chan's mirror short-on-gap 'failed to reproduce'; per the l3a0 page the mirror was profitable pre-cost (APR 12.2%, Sharpe 1.79) but did not match the published 46%/1.27 (see S016). Five up closes below the 200-day SMA is a bear-market rally where short-term momentum (S100) and squeeze risk dominate; borrow data is absent (G-09). Run once as the short counterpart to S030 under borrow scenarios (0.3% / 3% / 10% annualised); drop if not significant after FDR. Falsification only.

strategies.name: 52-Week-High Proximity Portfolio (George-Hwang)
strategies.concept: Nearness to the 52-week high is a stronger predictor of future returns than conventional momentum (George & Hwang 2004): the anchor biases sellers into trading too early, so stocks near their high keep grinding up.
strategies.indicators: close / 252-day high ratio
strategies.entry: Each month, rank stocks by close / 252-day-high ratio and buy the top decile (rank rule, primary), equal-weight, with a minimum ratio of 0.8 as a registered variant (a fixed 0.95 level selects far more than 10% of names in bull markets and far fewer in bear markets)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly; George-Hwang holding variant: skip a month, hold six months with overlapping cohorts
strategies.sources: George & Hwang (2004), The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing, J. Finance (not retrievable in review); Attached paper (user upload) - Borsa Istanbul (52-week-high characteristic: best single-characteristic net Sharpe 1.35 / CAGR 29.2%, but the paper stresses the ranking is noise, p = 0.12, and warns about retrospective discovery); Be The Puck stock-level 52-week-high scorecard (69/370 beat buy-and-hold Sharpe)
strategies.notes: The Trading Garden page cited earlier tests a 252-day-high BREAKOUT on the S&P cash index, i.e. S033, not a decile portfolio, and is no longer cited here. Highly collinear with S041 momentum: report the correlation (G-10). Benchmark: vol-matched equal-weight universe.
strategies.parameter_variants: selection {top decile by rank primary; ratio >= 0.8 floor}; holding {1 month primary; 6 months overlapping with 1-month skip}

strategies.name: 52-Week-High Breakout (Donchian-style)
strategies.concept: Buy at a new 252-day high, exit at a 126-day low — a slow breakout system; documented max single-trade loss 12.9% (max MAE) in the Trading Garden test.
strategies.universe: primary: sector/asset ETF set and liquid_top_N stocks (pooled trades and effective sample size); reference: SPY / S&P index (via MES in the source)
strategies.indicators: 252-day rolling high; 126-day rolling low
strategies.entry: Close(t) = 252-day closing high; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close = 126-day closing low; sell at close of that session
strategies.frequency: ~1-3 new positions per year on the index; run across sector ETFs and stocks for frequency
strategies.notes: Trading Garden (vendor AVALONPLUS comparison, S&P cash index/MES, sized by max MAE): 31 trades 1963-today, 71% win, CAGR 11.0% vs 10.9% buy-and-hold, worst single-trade loss 12.9% (max MAE), but only 14 trades since 2000 (CAGR 16.0% reinvested on MES): no statistical power on an index alone; it adds value as a regime overlay or when run across many ETFs/stocks. Compare with 200-day SMA timing as the null. The 63-day-high / 21-day-low fast variant is a second registered trial.
strategies.parameter_variants: speed {252-day high / 126-day low primary; 63-day high / 21-day low}

strategies.name: Low-Volatility Anomaly Portfolio
strategies.concept: Low-volatility stocks earn risk-adjusted returns at least as high as high-volatility stocks (leverage-constraint effect, Frazzini-Pedersen; Novy-Marx & Velikov attribute much of the anomaly to non-transparent equal-weighting, so the benchmark choice decides the result). The attached Borsa paper's finding is that ALL characteristics are redundant against an equal-weight, vol-matched universe, not that low-vol specifically is.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks: N=500 primary; N=100 (the paper's top-100-by-60-day-median-traded-value universe) as a variant
strategies.indicators: 252-trading-day annualized std of daily returns (primary); 60-day std (variant); beta vs SPY (variant)
strategies.entry: Each month, buy the lowest-volatility decile (lowest 252-day vol), equal-weight
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.sources: Attached paper (user upload) - Multi-Factor Investing in Borsa Istanbul (low-vol = minus the annualised std over the last 252 trading days, eq. 1); Frazzini & Pedersen (2014); Novy-Marx & Velikov
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the paper uses 252-day vol on a top-100 liquid universe (ranked by 60-day median traded value); the 60-day vol appears only as the vol-targeting estimator for the whole book. Paper numbers: pure low-vol net Sharpe 1.07 / CAGR 21.8% / max drawdown -66.8% in lira terms, USD Sharpe 0.13; the sector-neutral run adds only +1.4% alpha (t = 0.48). Low-vol deciles are utilities/staples/REIT heavy (2022 rate sensitivity, sector concentration). Benchmark: vol-matched equal-weight universe, not just the cap-weighted index.
strategies.parameter_variants: vol window {252-day primary, 60-day}; universe N {500 primary, 100}; sector-neutral {off primary, on}; low-beta decile (shrunk 252-day beta = 0.6 x beta_ts + 0.4, beta-scaled to 1) as a variant
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + SPY (DP-ETF) for the beta variant

strategies.name: Donchian Breakout, Turtle Systems 1 and 2 (absorbs S037)
strategies.concept: Entering on an N-day high breakout captures the start of multi-week trends; the shorter opposite-extreme exit cuts losers fast; unit sizing normalizes volatility. Turtle returns came from a diversified futures book (rates, FX, commodities); on equity-only ETFs this is mostly whipsaw long-equity beta, so the universe must be diversified. Run as ONE family with speeds {20, 55}.
strategies.universe: diversified ETF set (equity SPY/QQQ/IWM, rates TLT/IEF, gold GLD, oil USO, USD UUP/dollar ETF, commodities GSG) plus sector ETFs; long-only and long-short reported separately
strategies.indicators: Donchian high/low; N = Wilder-smoothed ATR, N_t = (19 x N_{t-1} + TR_t)/20 (alpha = 1/20, not an EMA with span 20); shadow-trade ledger for the System 1 filter
strategies.entry: System 1 (speed 20): close(t) > max high over sessions t-20..t-1 (EXCLUDING the current session); skip the breakout if the last breakout (real or shadow) would have been a winner. System 2 (speed 55): close(t) > max high over t-55..t-1, no last-trade filter. Unit size = 1% equity / (N x point value), capped at the per-position limit of the account; fill at next open
strategies.exit: System 1: close < 10-day low; System 2: close < 20-day low; mandatory 2N stop from entry (fill = min(open, stop)); mirror for shorts
strategies.frequency: ~2-6 trades per year per instrument; run across 10-20 ETFs for weekly frequency
strategies.notes: Kagels and Be The Puck agree with the rules (20-day entry / 10-day exit, N = 20-day ATR average, 1% risk per N, skip the breakout if the last would have won, out on a close below the prior 10-day low or 2N below entry). Be The Puck results: single stocks 62/372 (S1) and 61/372 (S2) beat buy-and-hold Sharpe; S&P 500 index CAGR +2.5% / +2.8% vs +8.9% (Sharpe 0.13 / 0.16 vs 0.45), long only. The Atlas (10.1, Kurth et al. 2026) finds short-term trend in ~100 futures stopped delivering since roughly 2009. Sizing at 1% equity / (N x point value) does not fit a $5,000 account with $1,000 positions. Trend-cluster control (with S033, S051, S091). Absorbs S037 (System 2); report the correlation between speeds.
strategies.parameter_variants: speed {20/10 System 1 primary; 55/20 System 2 (ex-S037)}; last-trade filter {on for speed 20, off for speed 55}; exit {channel exit primary; chandelier 3 x ATR(22) (see S091)}; direction {long-only, long-short}
strategies.data_needs: ETF total-return daily series incl. TLT, GLD, USO, GSG, dollar ETF (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: NR7 / Inside-Day Breakout (absorbs S039)
strategies.concept: Toby Crabel's compression idea: the narrowest range of 7 sessions (or an inside day) precedes expansion; buying the break of the setup bar's high (or shorting the low break) trades the direction of the resolution.
strategies.indicators: 7-day rolling range (NR7 test); inside-day test (high < prior high, low > prior low)
strategies.entry: On a setup session (NR7 or inside day), place a buy stop at the setup bar's high and a sell stop at its low for the next session; the first stop touched enters; cancel both if neither is touched. Stop-entry fills follow max(open, level) for buys and min(open, level) for sells (gap-aware). If BOTH levels trade in the session, the direction is the one whose stop is nearer the session OPEN; if exactly equidistant, skip
strategies.exit: Flatten on the close after 2 sessions (primary baseline). Registered exits: first profitable close (Crabel); opposite break; stop_target (ex-S039: stop at the opposite side of the NR7 bar, target 2 x initial risk, notional capped at the account's per-position limit)
strategies.frequency: several setups per week across a liquid universe
strategies.sources: [Fractiz - NR7 / inside day breakout rules](https://www.fractiz.com/strategies/nr7-inside-breakout/); StockCharts ChartSchool (Crabel's setup is an opening-range breakout with profits taken at the close of the first day or first profitable close); Validated Strategies NR7 page (https://validatedstrategies.com/strategy/nr7-xauusd) returned HTTP 404 in review, so the PF 0.64 gold claim is unverifiable
strategies.notes: Fractiz's sample runs (2020-2024, daily futures) show weak edges and ~40% drawdowns: NQ win 44%, PF 1.04, max drawdown 40.6%; ES PF 1.21, DD 39.3%; GC PF 1.39, DD 38.4% (154-163 trades). Be The Puck NR7: S&P 500 index -2.1%/yr vs +8.9%, beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 52/372. Holding two sessions differs from Crabel's quick exit. NR7 or inside day, both sides, doubles the trial count. Falsification test: require a positive net PF with the bootstrap CI lower bound > 1. Absorbs S039 (stop and 2R target as an exit variant; a stop at the opposite side of an NR7 bar is typically 0.3-0.8% of price, so '1% equity risk' sizing would imply 1.3-3x notional and the cap makes the 1% risk fictional).
strategies.parameter_variants: setup {NR7 or inside day; NR7 only; inside day only}; exit {2-session flatten primary; first profitable close; opposite break; stop + 2R target (ex-S039)}

strategies.name: Volume-Confirmed 20-Day-High Breakout
strategies.concept: New highs on above-median volume are institutional accumulation; volume separates genuine breakouts from stop-hunts.
strategies.indicators: 20-day rolling high of highs; ATR(14); 20-day median volume
strategies.entry: Close(t) > 20-day high AND close(t) - 20-day high > 0.1 x ATR(14) AND volume(t) vs 20-day median volume in one of two registered regimes (> 1.5x primary; < 1.0x quiet breakout); gap guard: skip if open(t+1) > close(t) + 1 x ATR(14), or enter by limit at close(t); buy at open of t+1
strategies.exit: Initial stop below breakout bar's low (fill = min(open, stop)); target 2 x initial risk or 8 sessions, whichever first
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.sources: [Kvants - Volume breakout strategy (generic framework article, no daily rules or numbers)](https://studio.kvants.ai/blog/volume-breakout-strategy)
strategies.notes: The Kvants page is a framework article ('a testable version must define the level, breakout distance, volume baseline...'); the parameters here (0.1 ATR, 1.5x median volume, 2R, 8 sessions) are the catalog's own, hence research-hypothesis. The Atlas (10.4, Mittal & Choudhary 2026) argues 'quiet-looking moves travel further than visually impressive breakouts', so both volume regimes are tested. Entering at the next open after a high-volume breakout carries gap risk. Be The Puck's 20-day-style rules (Four-Week Rule 74/372; Bollinger Breakout 54/372) are mediocre vs buy-and-hold.
strategies.parameter_variants: volume regime {> 1.5x median primary; < 1.0x median}; entry {next open primary with gap guard; limit at close(t)}

strategies.name: 12-1 Cross-Sectional Momentum
strategies.concept: The canonical academic momentum: rank stocks on returns from t-12 months to t-1 month (skipping the recent month to avoid the reversal window); buy winners. Chan confirms the standard lookback of ~11 of the last 12 months.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks (PIT rule, price >= $5, delisting returns applied); research scale: top decile; paper scale ($5,000): top-10
strategies.indicators: 12-1 month total-return rank (return from t-252 to t-21 sessions)
strategies.entry: At each month-end close, buy the top-decile 12-1 return stocks (top-10 at paper scale), equal-weight
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.sources: [Better System Trader — Ernie Chan interview (momentum lookback)](https://bettersystemtrader.com/012-ernest-chan/); [Jegadeesh-Titman 1993 (via Bauer College)](https://www.bauer.uh.edu/rsusmel/phd/jegadeesh-titman93.pdf)
strategies.notes: Chan interview: standard momentum lookback is roughly 11 of the most recent 12 months; Jegadeesh & Titman 1993 (formation J and holding K of 3-12 months; one-week gap between formation and holding in their main tests). Be The Puck 12-1 momentum beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 120/369, the best of its momentum family. Crash exposure: a long-only top decile is far less crash-prone than long-short but 2009 and 2020 rebounds hit it (overlays: S104). Required comparisons: vs random 10-stock placebo and vs the vol-matched equal-weight universe (the Borsa appendix: momentum as a negative control, random placebo beat residual momentum in 99.3% of draws, winners were high-vol stocks); industry-neutral variant (industry momentum drives much of stock momentum, Moskowitz-Grinblatt).
strategies.parameter_variants: breadth {top decile research; top-10 paper}; industry-neutral {off primary, on}; overlay {none primary; S104 gate; vol-scaling}

strategies.name: Sector Momentum Rotation
strategies.concept: Momentum works at the sector level with less idiosyncratic noise: hold the 3 strongest of 10 US equity sectors by 12-month momentum, rebalance monthly.
strategies.universe: SPDR sector ETFs from the PIT sector universe table (9/10/11 ETFs by date, XLK/XLC reconstitution noted)
strategies.indicators: 12-month trailing return rank
strategies.entry: At month-end, equal-weight the top 3 sector ETFs by 12-month total return (primary)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly; replace any sector that exits the top 3
strategies.notes: Quantpedia: ten sector ETFs, top 3 by 12-month momentum, monthly; its backtests (Faber, French-Fama sector data back to the 1920s) 'explicitly exclude taxes, commissions and slippage' and quote 100-400% annual turnover; the 1/3/6/9/12 grid with breadth 1-9 is dozens of trials in the source itself. Faber's data were French sectors, not ETFs. Benchmarks: equal-weight sector basket and SPY. Costs per the shared spec. S048 is registered as a variant of this entry.
strategies.parameter_variants: signal {12-month primary; combined 1/3/6/9/12 average rank}; breadth {top 3 primary}
strategies.data_needs: sector ETF total-return daily series (DP-ETF) + PIT sector universe table

strategies.name: ETF Multi-Asset Momentum Rotation (absorbs S068, S074)
strategies.concept: Rank a fixed multi-asset ETF universe by 12-month return; hold the top funds; rotate to short-term Treasuries when an ETF's 12-month return is negative (absolute momentum overlay).
strategies.universe: one ETF per asset class (primary): SPY, EFA, EEM, IWM or QQQ (single extra equity), TLT or IEF, LQD or HYG, GLD, GSG/DBC, IYR; SHY as cash floor. The earlier 13-ETF list had five US-equity-beta ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM, XLK, XLE) and was mostly equity rotation
strategies.indicators: 12-month total return rank (primary); close/SMA(200) - 1 (variant); SHY/BIL total return as cash floor
strategies.entry: At month-end, hold the top 5 ETFs by 12-month total return, equal-weight; replace any pick with a negative 12-month return by SHY
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.sources: [PortfoliosLab - Momentum & sector rotation strategies](https://portfolioslab.com/strategies/momentum-rotation) (describes sector/industry/factor rotation only; the top-ranked-funds/Treasury-replacement mechanics are supported, the 13-ETF multi-asset universe and Antonacci framing are the catalog's); CXO SACEMS and GEM are the established multi-asset comparators; phuazz breadth-thrust-etf (sleeve B, for the MA-distance signal)
strategies.notes: Benchmarks: equal-weight of the same ETFs and 60/40; SHY must be total return. Absorbs S068 (percent-above-200MA rotation: price distance above the 200-day MA is highly collinear with 12-month return rank; the source's 13-line sleeve is hand-picked, so pre-register the universe before running) and S074 (SPY/QQQ relative rotation, a two-asset instance: hold QQQ if QQQ 21-day return > SPY 21-day return AND the QQQ/SPY 63-day z-score > 0, else SPY; two heavily overlapping ETFs, evidence nil, no separate golden).
strategies.parameter_variants: signal {12-month return primary; ma200_distance = close/SMA200 - 1 (ex-S068: weekly, top 7, weighted by signal share, SHY for empty slots)}; universe {asset-class set primary; two-asset SPY/QQQ (ex-S074, weekly, 21-day return + 63-day z-score)}; rebalance {monthly primary; weekly}

strategies.name: Efficiente 5 MPT Replication
strategies.concept: JPMorgan's rules-based tactical ETF strategy: monthly, compute 6-month (126-day) mean returns and covariance of 13 ETFs, select the efficient portfolio targeting 5% volatility, subject to per-asset and asset-class caps and 5%-multiple weights. Short lookback makes it a momentum-flavored MPT rotation.
strategies.universe: SPY, IWM, EFA, TLT, LQD, HYG, EEM, EMB, IYR, GSG, GLD, TIP, BIL
strategies.indicators: 126-day mean return vector; 126-day covariance matrix; 5% volatility target; asset-class caps (equity 50%, bonds 50%, EM 25%, alternatives 25%, TIP/cash 50%)
strategies.entry: At each month-end, solve the constrained optimization: maximize return s.t. portfolio vol = 5% (escalate the target by 1% steps if infeasible; else minimum variance), weights in 5% multiples, per-asset caps (SPY 20, IWM 10, EFA 20, TLT 20, LQD 20, HYG 20, EEM 20, EMB 20, IYR 20, GSG 10, GLD 10, TIP 50, BIL 50) and class caps (developed equity 50%, bonds 50%, EM 25%, alternatives 25%); implement as a continuous solve followed by constrained rounding/local search (an integer program, not scipy-plus-rounding); portfolio is an excess return over BIL (funded by a short cash position)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly to the new solution
strategies.sources: Attached paper (user upload) — Institutional Asset Allocation meets the Efficient Frontier (JPM Efficiente 5 replication)] — attached PDF (user upload), no public URL verified
strategies.notes: Verified against the attached PDF (Jungle Rock Capital, Oct 2025): universe and caps match Table 1; monthly rebalance, 126-day average return and covariance. Published acceptance targets (replication Aug-2008 to Aug-2025, Yahoo data): average excess return 3.49% vs 2.89% actual, vol 6.23%, Sharpe 0.58 (actual 0.50), Sortino 0.79, max drawdown -19.07% (actual -16.56%), average monthly turnover 42.48%, correlation with the real index 0.94, tracking error 1.48%. Table 3 (5% target): weekly rebalance with 6-month lookback Sharpe 0.52, monthly 6-month 0.61, monthly 12-month 0.55; at a 10% target the caps bind and realised vol stays ~8%. Sharpe 0.5-0.6 is the PUBLISHED performance (a Sharpe > 2 gate would reject it). Acceptance on the framework's 2016+ data: constraints satisfied every month, subperiod stats consistent with Table 2, qualitative average-weights-by-year pattern; full numeric replication only in 'replication' mode on 2008-2025 Yahoo data. Monthly turnover of 42% x 5-10 bps is a ~2-5%/yr drag: report net. Use as the first end-to-end golden of the slow-sleeve pipeline; unit tests for the cap constraints and the 1%-step escalation. The '(pypfopt)' remark is from the paper's footnote 3, not a requirement.
strategies.parameter_variants: mode {replication: Yahoo 2008-2025 matching Tables 2-3; catalog: framework data}; lookback {126-day primary; 6-month/12-month, weekly rebalance (Table 3)}; target vol {5% primary; 10%}
strategies.data_needs: 13 ETFs with dividends from 2008 for replication (Yahoo/Stooq one-off); DP-ETF for the framework window; BIL (FRED T-bill before 2007)
strategies.review: KEEP (pipeline replication test) | source OK (verified against attached PDF)

strategies.name: Multi-Factor Characteristic Blend (US Adaptation; S045a paper design, S045b catalog design)
strategies.concept: The attached Borsa Istanbul paper blends 5 characteristics — low volatility, value (5-year reversal proxy), 52-week-high proximity, 1-month reversal, and quality — into a 10-stock portfolio with volatility targeting and a trend gate. Adapting the price-only characteristics to US stocks is a direct implementation of the paper's design minus the fundamentals.
strategies.indicators: S045a: composite of z-scores of low volatility (252-day), value (5-year reversal proxy), 52-week-high proximity, 1-month reversal (quality omitted: fundamentals); 60-day realized vol for vol targeting; SMA(200) and vol quintile for the regime gate. S045b: 60-day volatility rank; close/252-day-high rank; 21-day reversal rank; SMA(200) market gate
strategies.entry: S045a (the paper's design): each month, composite-rank the universe on the price characteristics, take the top 20 by composite, then the lower-volatility half = 10 names; rank buffer (incumbents kept while in the top 30); scale gross exposure to a 20% vol target from 60-day realised vol, capped at 100%; three-state trend/regime gate with multipliers 1.00 / 0.70 / 0.40 (SPY vs its 200-day average and vol quintile); 25 bps costs. S045b (the catalog's simplified version): composite of the 3 price characteristics, buy the top 10 equal-weight only when SPY > SMA200 (else cash), 20% target vol
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.sources: Attached paper (user upload) — Multi-Factor Investing in Borsa Istanbul] — attached PDF (user upload), no public URL verified
strategies.notes: The attached paper's own conclusion: Sharpe 1.19 vs 0.89 for the cap-weighted index but alpha -0.4%/yr (95% CI [-6.3%, +5.5%]) against a vol-matched equal-weight universe; levels are 'in-sample-flattered'; ~57% monthly turnover. The vol-matched equal-weight benchmark is a REQUIRED output column; interpret any result below benchmark + 0.15 Sharpe as 'no selection skill'. S045b deviates from the paper (drops value, replaces the three-state gate with a binary one, drops the buffer and the low-vol tilt, uses top-10 directly); the old 4-indicator cap is no longer a constraint. The Efficiente 5 paper is NOT a source for this entry.
strategies.parameter_variants: design {S045a paper design primary; S045b catalog simplification}

strategies.name: Industry Rotation via Market-State Similarity
strategies.concept: Zakamulin: find historical months whose standardized market return is closest to the current month; long industries that historically rose after similar states, short those that fell. Predictability concentrates in the tails (down markets).
strategies.universe: Ken French 49-industry monthly portfolios (free, 1926+; re-verify the URL) for the replication; then sector ETFs (ETF history since 1998 gives ~330 months, so analog counts are a large share of history)
strategies.indicators: standardized market excess return; historical analog matching
strategies.entry: At each month-end, find the K closest historical analog months by standardized market return (K = 50 primary; registered {25, 50, 100}); long the top-tercile industries by subsequent historical return, short the bottom tercile (shorting is required for the tail effect the paper cites)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.sources: [Papers With Backtest — Industry Rotation Using Market-State Similarity](https://paperswithbacktest.com/strategies/industry-rotation-using-market-state-similarity)
strategies.notes: The cited page is Zakamulin's abstract (May 2026): monthly French industry portfolios, quantile predictability concentrated in the tails, a market-state similarity strategy with 'higher Sharpe, lower volatility, substantially smaller drawdowns than the passive equal-weighted industry benchmark'. The '50 closest analogs' and 'top/bottom tercile' parameters are NOT in the abstract (catalog's own). Replicate on French data first, then port to ETFs.
strategies.parameter_variants: analog count K {50 primary, 25, 100}; legs {long-short primary; long-only}
strategies.data_needs: Ken French 49-industry data (external one-off); sector ETF series (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: Absolute / Dual Momentum (S047a absolute SPY vs cash; S047b Antonacci GEM)
strategies.concept: S047a: if SPY's 12-month return beats the 12-month cash (T-bill) return, hold SPY for the next month, else cash (Trading Garden / Antonacci absolute momentum). S047b: Antonacci's GEM (dual momentum): relative step US vs ex-US equities, then absolute step vs T-bills, else aggregate bonds (AGG) / BIL. A single-asset trend/momentum gate that avoids bear markets.
strategies.universe: S047a: SPY, cash (BIL; FRED 3-month T-bill before 2007). S047b: SPY, EFA or ACWX, AGG, BIL
strategies.indicators: 12-month total return of SPY (and EFA/ACWX); 12-month T-bill return
strategies.entry: S047a: at month-end, if SPY 12-month return > 12-month T-bill return hold SPY the next month, else hold cash. S047b: at month-end pick the higher of SPY and EFA/ACWX by 12-month return; if it also beats T-bills hold it, else hold AGG (BIL as alternate)
strategies.exit: Rebalance monthly
strategies.notes: The earlier rule (SPY -> TLT -> cash) was neither the Trading Garden rule ('long for the whole next month if the 12-month return beats the 12-month cash rate') nor GEM; the TLT fallback adds duration risk (2022) and is now a registered variant of S047a. Trading Garden results (S&P/MES): 1963-today 35 trades, 68.6% win, CAGR 11.5% vs 10.9%; only 15 trades since 2000. Trade count is tiny (G-05): use as the most robust crash filter/overlay for faster strategies. Comparator: Faber 10-month SMA gate (price vs 10-month SMA, total return, monthly).
strategies.parameter_variants: variant {S047a SPY vs cash primary; S047b GEM}; defensive asset {cash primary; TLT (ex-original S047); AGG}; comparator {10-month SMA gate}
strategies.data_needs: SPY, EFA/ACWX, AGG, BIL total-return series + FRED T-bill (DP-ETF, DP-FRED)

strategies.name: Validea Short-Term Sector Momentum
strategies.concept: Hold the 5 strongest of 10 sector ETFs ranked by multiple momentum metrics; documented 11.2% annual return since 2006 vs 10.9% for the S&P 500, beta 0.88.
strategies.indicators: multi-metric momentum rank (e.g., 1-month and 3-month return blend)
strategies.entry: At each rebalance (test weekly and monthly), buy the top 5 sector ETFs by blended 1M+3M return, equal-weight
strategies.exit: Rebalance on the fixed schedule
