Validea's page confirms 'Since 2006... 11.2%' vs S&P 500 10.9%, beta 0.88, standard deviation 19.0%, but its disclaimer says the optimal portfolios 'represent the rebalancing period that has led to the best historical performance... determined after the fact' and 'model returns... do not reflect actual trading': the headline is selected with hindsight, and 11.2% at beta 0.88 against 10.9% is only ~+1.6%/yr of alpha before costs. The 1M+3M blend and the weekly/monthly schedule are the catalog's choices. Benchmark vs equal-weight sectors.

strategies.name: Acceleration Momentum
strategies.concept: Second-order momentum: stocks whose recent 1-month return exceeds their average monthly pace over the prior year are accelerating; acceleration adds cross-sectional information beyond level momentum.
strategies.indicators: 21-day return; 252-day return; acceleration = r21 - r252/12 (difference, or cross-sectional ranks); the ratio r21/(r252/12) explodes when r252 is near zero and is not used
strategies.entry: At each week's end, buy the decile with the highest acceleration (r21 - r252/12) among stocks with positive 252-day return; run weekly and monthly
strategies.exit: Rebalance weekly
strategies.sources: Chan interview (momentum lookbacks only, no acceleration concept): https://bettersystemtrader.com/012-ernest-chan/
strategies.notes: Falsification: the numerator is the last 21-day return, i.e. a 1-month WINNER screen, the sign S027/S028 (and the NY Fed paper) say reverses; the two effects point in opposite directions and the hypothesis needs a theory for when acceleration dominates reversal. Pre-register S028 as the control; drop if it does not beat the inverted S028 reversal. A weekly decile rebalance of liquid names is expensive (G-08). The Chan interview does not discuss acceleration.
strategies.parameter_variants: measure {r21 - r252/12 primary; cross-sectional rank difference}; rebalance {weekly, monthly}

strategies.name: First Pullback After Breakout
strategies.concept: After a new 63-day high, the first 3-day pullback to the 10-day SMA is the highest-probability continuation entry — momentum pauses, profit-takers exit to momentum buyers.
strategies.indicators: 63-day rolling high; 10-day SMA; 3-day pullback count
strategies.entry: Stock made a 63-day high within the last 10 sessions, then closes 3 consecutive sessions lower with each close within 2% of the 10-day SMA; buy at close of the third session
strategies.exit: Close > breakout bar's high (the 63-day-high bar's high, fixed at breakout; continuation confirmed) or close < 20-day SMA; max hold 10 sessions; report the exit-type distribution (most trades otherwise exit at the time stop)
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.notes: Parameters 63/10/3/2% are all free: run a coarse grid with full trial accounting, not the single (63, 10, 3, 2%) point. A price within 2% of its 10-day SMA after 3 down closes can only exceed the breakout high within 10 sessions if the pullback was shallow. The cited Kvants page has no rules or numbers (decorative citation, see S040). Report with and without earnings-window signals (G-12).
strategies.parameter_variants: grid {breakout lookback 42/63/126; pullback days 2/3/4; SMA distance 1%/2%/3%} (all registered trials)

strategies.name: Darvas Box Breakout
strategies.concept: Nicolas Darvas' 1950s system, in its usual mechanical form: a 'box' top is a high that is not beaten for three days; the box bottom is a low that holds for the three days after that; buy a close above the box top.
strategies.indicators: Darvas box top (high unbeaten for 3 sessions) and box bottom (low unbeaten for the following 3 sessions)
strategies.entry: Close(t) > current box top; buy at close of t (fill at next open as alternate)
strategies.exit: Close < the latest box bottom (which ratchets up as new boxes form); no profit target
strategies.sources: Be The Puck - Darvas box scorecard (mechanical definition above; beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 44/372; S&P 500 index +4.3%/yr vs +8.9%); the Kagels Turtle page cited earlier contains no Darvas rule and is no longer cited
strategies.notes: REPLACED: the earlier '55-day range unexceeded for 15+ sessions' mixed two windows and was an arbitrary range breakout (a close cousin of S036), with a stray non-English typo in the notes (fixed). The three-day box is the Be The Puck mechanical definition; Darvas' original rules were discretionary.

strategies.name: Earnings Announcement Premium (Monthly; absorbs S086 weekly version)
strategies.concept: Frazzini-Lamont (NBER w13090): stocks expected to announce earnings in month t outperform stocks not announcing; the strategy buys every expected announcer at the last close of month t-1 and shorts non-announcers.
strategies.universe: US stocks with exactly 4 announcements in the prior 12 months (expected dates from SimFin Publish Date, 2009+; ~2/3 of stocks announce in any month)
strategies.direction: long and short (long-only version: just hold announcers)
strategies.indicators: expected earnings calendar for month t (prior-year pattern); past announcement-period volume concentration (Frazzini-Lamont main cross-sectional result)
strategies.entry: On the last trading day of month t-1, buy all stocks expected to announce in month t (equal-weight at paper scale, value-weight at research scale), sorted by past announcement-period volume concentration (high-volume names earn the highest premium); short non-announcers (long-only variant: long announcers only, market-neutralized with an SPY short)
strategies.exit: Hold through the last trading day of month t; reform monthly. Weekly version (ex-S086): single exit rule = hold the weekly basket for one week
strategies.sources: [NBER w13090 — The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w13090/w13090.pdf)
strategies.notes: NBER w13090 (Frazzini & Lamont) verified: 'exactly four earnings announcements' restriction, long expected announcers / short non-announcers, value-weighted monthly, 61 bps/month long-short, Sharpe 0.94 vs 0.70 for momentum; stocks with high past announcement-period volume earn the highest premium. The sample ends in the early 2000s; the premium after publication is untested in the cited paper, so report subperiods. This is an earnings-calendar strategy only: no LLM or news input. Absorbs S086 (weekly tilt: in weeks 3-4 of each fiscal quarter, buy the equal-weight basket of stocks expected to announce that week from prior-year timing, +/-1 week of jitter; the earlier version had two conflicting exit rules, now one).
strategies.parameter_variants: cadence {monthly primary; weekly ex-S086 (weeks 3-4 of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct)}; weighting {equal paper, value research}; sort {volume concentration primary; none}; leg {long announcers - SPY hedge primary; long-short}

strategies.name: Pre-Earnings Run-Up (consensus-free; replaces the Earnings Whispers Score setup)
strategies.concept: Frazzini-Lamont's announcement premium accrues in the days before and at the announcement and is largest for stocks with high past announcement-period volume. A consensus-free pre-earnings run-up replaces the proprietary Earnings Whispers Score (no free history), and the exit explicitly INCLUDES the earnings reaction.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks with SimFin Publish Date history
strategies.indicators: days to the expected announcement (prior-year Publish Date pattern); past announcement-period volume concentration (top tercile)
strategies.entry: Buy a stock 5-7 sessions before its expected earnings announcement when it is in the top tercile of past announcement-period volume concentration
strategies.exit: Sell at the open after the announcement (this INCLUDES the earnings gap for both after-close and pre-market reporters); the window ends at that open
strategies.sources: [Earnings Whispers - Scoring Expectations to Capture the Earnings Announcement Premium (vendor context: +1.08% for Score +5 vs +0.47% all others, about a week before to the open after, 11,385 events, Apr-2014 to Oct-2026)](https://www.earningswhispers.com/about-score); [NBER w13090 - Frazzini & Lamont](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w13090/w13090.pdf)
strategies.notes: RESOLVED (was BLOCKED): the proprietary Score has no free history and the 'Score > +2' threshold is not even on the vendor page, so the entry is rebuilt on public data (SimFin Publish Date from 2009, prices from daily_10years). Even the vendor's Score +5 edge is only ~0.6% over six sessions before costs on a vendor-selected sample. Weekly version of S052, run in parallel with it; the earlier claim of exiting 'before the reaction risk' was wrong and is removed.
strategies.parameter_variants: entry offset {5-7 sessions before primary; 1 week before}; sort {volume concentration top tercile primary; none}

strategies.name: PEAD Earnings-Surprise Drift (SUE / announcement-return, point-in-time)
strategies.concept: Stocks with the largest positive earnings surprises keep drifting for weeks as investors underreact. Surprise is measured consensus-free, as in Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok (1996, verify): SUE from reported EPS and the announcement-window abnormal return (EAR).
strategies.direction: long (and optional short leg for big misses)
strategies.indicators: SUE = (EPS_q - EPS_{q-4}) / std of the last 8 such differences (seasonal random walk, SimFin quarterly EPS); EAR = cumulative return t-1..t+1 around the release minus SPY; trailing-cutoff percentile
strategies.entry: After a positive surprise whose SUE is above the top-decile cutoff computed from the PREVIOUS four quarters' pooled surprises (trailing/expanding distribution; never the same-season cross-section, which contains announcements that have not happened yet), buy at the open of the first session after the reaction session (t+1 after a BMO report, t+2 after an AMC report; BMO/AMC from EDGAR 8-K 2.02 acceptance time, 2023-09+)
strategies.exit: Hold 10 sessions (primary) or until the next earnings announcement; 21 sessions registered alternate
strategies.frequency: concentrated in earnings seasons (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct)
strategies.sources: Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996) (verify); [NBER w13090 - announcement premium (about announcement-period returns, not drift)](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w13090/w13090.pdf); Earnings Whispers page (announcement premium, vendor); Martineau 'Rest in Peace PEAD' (verify) on the large-cap decay after 2000
strategies.notes: FIXED: the original 'top decile of the quarter's surprises' ranked announcements against all announcements in the season, including future ones (look-ahead). Neither the Earnings Whispers page nor NBER w13090 is about post-announcement drift. No consensus estimates are available, so SUE + EAR are the surprise measures. PEAD in large caps is thought to have weakened sharply after 2000: test the post-2016 sample before relying on it. Long-only first; the short leg for big misses is a separate experiment (G-09). Matched size/industry controls and subperiods required.
strategies.parameter_variants: surprise measure {SUE top decile primary; EAR top decile; both (SUE and EAR top decile)}; hold {10 primary, 21, 42}; leg {long primary; short bottom decile separate}
strategies.data_needs: SimFin quarterly EPS + Publish Date; EDGAR 8-K 2.02 timestamps 2023-09+ (DP-EARN); daily_10years (D1)

strategies.name: Post-Earnings-Oversold Bounce
strategies.concept: A stock that drops sharply on earnings but remains in a long-term uptrend (above 200-day SMA) typically recovers part of the drop within days — earnings-gap dislocation + regime filter.
strategies.indicators: earnings-day return; SMA(200); RSI(2)
strategies.entry: Reaction session defined from the filing timestamp (BMO: same day; AMC: next day). On the first session after the reaction session, if the stock fell more than 7% on the reaction AND close > SMA200 AND RSI(2) < 10; buy at close of that session (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA; sell at close of that session; max 5 sessions
strategies.sources: [Be The Puck - ConnorsRSI pullback (plain ConnorsRSI rule, not an earnings strategy)](https://bethepuck.com/strategies/connorsrsi-pullback/); Chan's Estimize post is not about earnings reversion
strategies.notes: Counter-hypothesis to S054, expected null: after a large negative surprise the literature expects drift DOWN, and S054's own premise is that surprises persist for weeks. Pair the long test with S054's short leg on the SAME events so the two hypotheses are tested against each other. Reaction day depends on BMO/AMC timing (2.02 timestamps 2023-09+ only, or the Alpaca news timestamp). A 7% drop with RSI(2) < 10 is many conditions for a handful of events per season.
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + EDGAR 8-K 2.02 timestamps / SimFin Publish Date (DP-EARN)

strategies.name: LLM Daily News Sentiment Long/Short
strategies.concept: arXiv 2412.19245 (Kirtac & Germano): daily LLM sentiment scores per stock from news; long the top-20% sentiment stocks, short the bottom-20%, rebalanced daily. The paper's best model is OPT (GPT-3-based; accuracy 74.4%, L-S Sharpe 3.05), then BERT 2.11 and FinBERT 2.07; the LM dictionary is lowest.
strategies.universe: US stocks with daily news coverage in data/pit/news/news.parquet (Alpaca/Benzinga, 2023-09 onward, ~75k rows, ~1,900 symbols); live capture for forward evidence
strategies.indicators: frozen FinBERT sentiment score (no fine-tuning on our window); quintile assignment; news-intensity z-score (see S060)
strategies.entry: Each day, score each stock's news with FinBERT and trade long the top quintile / short the bottom quintile, value-weighted and size-neutralised, costs 10 bps per trade. Timing: news before 6am -> trade at that day's open and CLOSE THE SAME DAY (the paper's branch); 6am-4pm news -> trade at that day's close and exit the next trading day (primary overnight convention); after 4pm -> next open. Long-only first
strategies.exit: Primary: next-open exit (overnight convention: close entry, next-open exit); the paper's same-day-close exit for pre-6am news is a registered branch
strategies.sources: [arXiv 2412.19245 - Sentiment trading with large language models](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19245); Lopez-Lira & Tang 2026 (Atlas 15.1); Roy & Roy 2026 (leakage audits)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the earlier 'FINBERT tested best' is wrong (OPT is best). LEAKAGE: the models were fine-tuned on an 80% random split of articles across 2010-2023, so the held-out 20% is interleaved in time with training data, and OPT is a GPT-3-class model whose pretraining covers most of the sample: Sharpe 3.05 (mean daily L-S return 0.55%, ~140%/yr) is not credible out of sample. Data: Refinitiv news + CRSP (commercial), 965,375 articles after a 0.8 cosine novelty filter. GPT-4 headline scores predict drift only AFTER the model cutoff, concentrated in small stocks and negative news, with returns declining as LLM adoption rises (Lopez-Lira & Tang 2026). Therefore: frozen 2019 FinBERT, evaluate ONLY on post-cutoff data (news.parquet from 2023-09 is entirely post-cutoff for FinBERT) or live capture; masked-ticker and cross-model disagreement checks; report IC decay by month.
strategies.parameter_variants: model {FinBERT frozen primary; LM dictionary baseline}; timing {close entry / next-open exit primary; pre-6am same-day branch}; legs {long-only primary; long-short}

strategies.name: LLM Top-Down Sector Allocation (forward test only)
strategies.concept: arXiv 2503.09647: an LLM Ranking Agent assesses macro conditions, sets overweight/underweight targets across the 11 GICS sectors, then selects stocks within targeted sectors using aspect-based sentiment.
strategies.indicators: LLM macro assessment (11-sector target weights); aspect sentiment scores
strategies.entry: FORWARD TEST ONLY (no backtest): weekly, prompt a FROZEN LLM with current macro data and news to produce sector weights across the 11 GICS sectors; rebalance a paper portfolio to those weights, selecting the highest aspect-sentiment stocks within each overweighted sector; capture raw model outputs with vendor and ingestion timestamps
strategies.exit: Rebalance on the fixed weekly schedule; evaluate after >= 6 months of paper trading before any capital
strategies.notes: RESOLVED as a forward test: the paper's backtest covers only January 2019 through June 2019 ('due to constraints on computational resources and cost'; 300,000 articles; 8.79% return, Sharpe 2.51 vs cross-momentum -1.39% / -0.61). The earlier '2019-2024' was wrong. Six months, one regime, and a frontier LLM that knows 2019 macro is no evidence, and every rebalance costs LLM calls, so the entry is removed from the backtest queue and run only as a live paper experiment with timestamped capture (existing Alpaca news client in src/data/news_client.py), score IC decay, and costs.
strategies.data_needs: live news capture (DP-NEWS live) + frozen model; no historical backtest possible

strategies.name: News-Topic Conditioned Sentiment (feature design for S056)
strategies.concept: Re-scoped: Kiszczuk (SSRN 7665703) is an explainability study (291,260 news summaries for S&P 500 firms; topics via FinBERT embeddings, PaCMAP and hierarchical clustering; topics more than double the within-R2 from 7.17% to 15.17% beyond sentiment; firm-specific and fundamental topics add most; 'reproduced financial intermediary information' adds little). It has NO trading rule or return forecast. The usable idea is a FEATURE for S056: sentiment conditioned on news topic.
strategies.universe: rated stock universe (paper uses news-covered stocks)
strategies.indicators: FinBERT embeddings of headline/summary; hierarchical clustering into topics; topic-conditioned FinBERT sentiment
strategies.entry: No standalone trading rule. Evaluation spec: cluster news items into topics, keep firm-specific/fundamental topics, drop analyst-rating-repeat topics, and test whether topic-conditioned sentiment has a higher information coefficient (IC) for next-session returns than raw sentiment on news.parquet (2023-09+); if yes, feed it into S056's score
strategies.exit: n/a
strategies.sources: Attached paper (user upload) - Opening the Black Box: Which News Explain LLM-Based Stock Ratings? (SSRN 7665703); the attached PDF is a single title page and SSRN also lists 1 page, so only the abstract was used
strategies.notes: RESOLVED by re-scope: the earlier 'rating upgrade + positive news -> buy' was the catalog's own placeholder, not derived from the paper. The full paper (if rules are wanted) must be requested from the author/SSRN.

strategies.name: Insider Cluster Buying
strategies.concept: Open-market insider buying by several distinct insiders signals undervaluation. Evidence base: a Northwestern thesis by John Ryle, CFA, published as a guest post on Chan's blog (~650,000 insider open-market buys, a random-forest model, 3-month return relative to the Russell 3000).
strategies.universe: US stocks with Form 4 filings (SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets, 2006+)
strategies.indicators: count of distinct insiders with open-market buys (transaction code P) in trailing 21 sessions, excluding routine (same-month-each-year) and 10b5-1 trades; filing acceptance time
strategies.entry: 3+ distinct insiders made open-market purchases (code P, non-routine, non-10b5-1) in the last 21 sessions, timed by Form 4 filing acceptance time (not trade date); buy at the close of the trigger session after the filing. Registered variant: additionally zero insider sells in the 21 sessions (very restrictive)
strategies.exit: Hold 63 sessions or exit on 20-day low; evaluate on relative return vs matched size/industry; effective sample size = sample length / 63
strategies.sources: [John Ryle (guest post on Ernest Chan's blog) - Building an Insider Trading Database and Predicting Future Equity Returns](http://epchan.blogspot.com/2017/07/building-insider-trading-database-and.html); Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012) opportunistic vs routine insider trades (verify)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: this is not Chan's research. The post documents a guest thesis whose random forest looked good in validation but in the 2014-2015 test 'the relationship broke down substantially... the actual returns on all remaining prediction deciles appeared no better than random; relative returns were negative for every decile'. No cluster rule is tested there, so the cluster rule, thresholds and exits are entirely the catalog's; the only documented evidence points to NO edge out of sample. Form 4 is not in the repo's EDGAR table (8-K, 10-Q, 13G, S-x only).
strategies.parameter_variants: cluster {>= 3 insiders primary; >= 3 and zero sells}; hold {63 sessions primary; 20-day-low exit}
strategies.data_needs: SEC Form 4 insider transactions bulk TSV 2006+ (DP-FORM4); daily_10years (D1)

strategies.name: News-Intensity Overnight Drift (conditioning feature of S056)
strategies.concept: Stocks with unusually high pre-market news flow and positive sentiment gap up and keep drifting for 1-3 days. Re-scoped as a news-intensity z-score conditioning feature of S056 and tested on the available archive.
strategies.indicators: pre-market news-item count vs trailing 20-day average (z-score; require a minimum count of 3 items given the sparse archive); frozen FinBERT polarity; gap vs ATR(20)
strategies.entry: Pre-market news count > 3 x its 20-day average (and >= 3 items) AND net frozen-FinBERT sentiment positive AND open gap < 2 x ATR (not exhausted); buy at the close of the 09:31 bar of t (an open-derived signal cannot fill at the open)
strategies.exit: Sell at close of t+2 or trail 2-bar low; max 3 sessions
strategies.notes: RESOLVED as a conditioning feature: no evidence exists for the standalone rule and the cited paper has no overnight-news result. The archive in the repo (news.parquet, ~75k rows from 2023-09, ~1,900 symbols) is too sparse for 15-year counts but is enough for a post-cutoff research test; item-count z-scores are noisy at ~40 items per symbol, hence the minimum-count requirement. Overlaps S056/S023. Same look-ahead hygiene as S056 (frozen FinBERT, post-cutoff windows).
strategies.data_needs: data/pit/news/news.parquet with timestamps (DP-NEWS, 2023-09+); daily_10years (D1) + 09:31 minute bars

strategies.name: VIX Spike Mean Reversion (SPY)
strategies.concept: VIX is strongly mean-reverting; extreme spikes (VIX > 30, or > 1.5 × its 20-day average) coincide with panic selling that reverts as vol normalizes. Buying SPY at extreme VIX buys maximum fear.
strategies.indicators: VIX level; VIX 20-day average; RSI(2); SMA(5)
strategies.entry: VIX(t) > T AND VIX(t) > 1.5 x 20-day average of VIX AND SPY RSI(2) < 10; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound). T = 30 primary; registered {25, 35}. Registered confirmation: VIX has turned down (VIX close < prior VIX close)
strategies.exit: VIX < 20 OR close > 5-day SMA (the SMA5 leg will dominate; the VIX leg rarely triggers); sell at close of that session; max 10 sessions
strategies.frequency: 2-6 trades per year (raise frequency by running on QQQ, IWM, and sector ETFs)
strategies.sources: [Papers With Backtest - Using VIX to trade SPY (general article: buy SPY when VIX is high, sell when low; no thresholds or results)](https://paperswithbacktest.com/strategies/using-vix-to-trade-spy-and-sp-500)
strategies.notes: The thresholds (VIX > 30, 1.5x 20-day average, RSI(2) < 10) are the catalog's own. Independent episodes with VIX > 30 in 2016-2026 are about 4-6 (Feb-2018, Dec-2018, Mar-Jun 2020, 2022, Apr-2025): a triple-conditioned rule has a handful of events, so report an event table with dates and make no significance claim. In sustained crises (2008-style) buying the first VIX > 30 close loses for months and the 2016+ sample omits that failure case, so validate pre-2016 with CBOE history (VIX from 1990, SPY 1993+) under the same rules. The 'VIX turned down' confirmation follows the Connors CVR3 idea (VIX bar rules: low above the 10-day MA, close >= 10% above it, black candle; sell on the mirror).
strategies.parameter_variants: VIX threshold {30 primary, 25, 35}; confirmation {none primary; VIX close < prior close}; universe {SPY primary; QQQ, IWM, sector ETFs}
strategies.data_needs: CBOE VIX daily 1990+ (DP-VIX) + SPY total-return series (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: VIX/VXV Ratio Spike (Term Structure)
strategies.concept: When the 30-day VIX exceeds the 3-month VIX3M (formerly VXV; ratio >= 1.10), near-term fear is extreme relative to the quarter view. Schaeffer's: 25 de-overlapped signals over nine years, average +1.94% (median 2.90%, 17 wins) per one-month hold, one 16.37% drawdown in 2008.
strategies.indicators: VIX / VIX3M ratio (VIX3M is the 2017 rename of VXV: splice the series; VIX9D/VIX is a DIFFERENT quantity and is not a substitute)
strategies.entry: VIX/VXV ratio closes at or above 1.10; buy SPY at close of t
strategies.exit: Hold one month (21 sessions); sell at close
strategies.sources: [Schaeffer's Research — Another Way to Trade Volatility (VXV)](https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/analysis/2015/12/03/another-way-to-trade-volatility)
strategies.notes: Selectively quoted earlier: across ALL 113 days with ratio >= 1.10 the average one-month forward return was 0.22% vs 0.75% for randomly timed holds (median 2.69% vs 1.49%), the correlation of the ratio with forward returns is 'an uninspiring 0.0324', and the author attributes the pattern to data overlaps intersecting with 2008; data begin mid-2006. 25 de-overlapped incidents dominated by 2008 is not a validated edge; since 2016 the incidents are likely under 10. Report BOTH all-days and incident-based statistics, include 2008 through CBOE history so the drawdown is in sample, and trial-count the 1.10 threshold. Signal counts must not overlap (Schaeffer's incident convention); run in parallel with S061 as one vol-timing basket.
strategies.parameter_variants: ratio threshold {1.10 primary; 1.05, 1.15}; statistics {all signal days and de-overlapped incidents}
strategies.data_needs: CBOE VIX + VIX3M/VXV history 2006+ (DP-VIX) + SPY total-return series

strategies.name: VIX Moving-Average Crossover Regime
strategies.concept: A short-term VIX MA crossing a long-term VIX MA marks vol-regime turns: falling short-term vol (risk appetite returning) → hold equities; rising → de-risk.
strategies.indicators: 20-day VIX MA; 50-day VIX MA
strategies.entry: 20-day VIX MA < 50-day VIX MA AND VIX falling (VIX(t) < VIX(t-5)); hold SPY
strategies.exit: 20-day VIX MA > 50-day VIX MA; move to cash
strategies.sources: [Papers With Backtest - Using VIX to trade SPY (shows a 20/50 VIX moving-average crossover as an example with sample code; no backtest results)](https://paperswithbacktest.com/strategies/using-vix-to-trade-spy-and-sp-500)
strategies.notes: The 'VIX falling over 5 days' condition is the catalog's. A VIX trend signal is mostly a trend-of-SPY signal and will be highly correlated with the 200-day SMA regime (S069/S089): compare against SMA200 timing and S069, and report incremental information by regressing the VIX-MA signal returns on the SMA200 signal. Combine with S047 as a dual-gate overlay only if incremental.

strategies.name: Hurst Exponent Regime Switch
strategies.concept: Chan's volatility term-structure method: compute variance of log returns at multiple horizons; the slope of log-variance vs log-horizon gives the Hurst exponent H. H < 0.5 = mean-reverting market (run mean-reversion strategies); H > 0.5 = trending (run momentum strategies).
strategies.universe: SPY, QQQ, and any traded ETF
strategies.indicators: Hurst exponent via a variance-ratio regression (log-variance vs log-horizon, horizons 1-64 days) with block-bootstrap confidence intervals; strategy-selection gate (inherits the indicators of S001 and S036)
strategies.entry: Each week, estimate H on the trailing 504 daily log returns (variance at horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 days) with a block-bootstrap CI; switch ONLY when the CI excludes 0.5: H CI entirely < 0.5 -> run RSI(2) mean reversion (S001) on the ETF; H CI entirely > 0.5 -> run Donchian 20 breakout (S036); otherwise hold cash. First evaluate regime persistence (autocorrelation of the regime label)
strategies.exit: Managed by the underlying strategy; re-evaluate regime weekly
strategies.frequency: weekly regime decision; trades from the underlying strategy
strategies.sources: [Ernest Chan — Mean reversion, momentum, and volatility term structure](http://epchan.blogspot.com/2016/04/mean-reversion-momentum-and-volatility.html)
strategies.notes: Chan's post (April 2016): SPY intraday H = 0.494 +/- 0.003, daily H (1-256 day variance, 2013-2016) = 0.469 +/- 0.007 ('significantly mean reverting'); USO daily H 0.56 (trending); GLD daily H 0.469; transition from momentum to mean reversion near 16-32 days. The post classifies INSTRUMENTS and does not propose a time-varying gate. With SPY's H near 0.47 the old fixed bands (< 0.45 / > 0.55) mostly output cash, and on a rolling 504-day window with horizons <= 64 the standard error is several times larger than the post's 0.007 (overlapping returns leave ~8 independent samples at the longest horizon). The realistic use is instrument-level classification (USO trending; GLD/SPY mean-reverting). The entry mixes two strategies whose own edges are unproven, adding trials multiplicatively.
strategies.parameter_variants: gate {CI excludes 0.5 primary; fixed bands 0.45/0.55}; use {rolling regime gate; static instrument-level classification}

strategies.name: Realized-Vol Compression Breakout (compression cluster champion candidate)
strategies.concept: When 5-day realized vol falls below half the 20-day realized vol, the market is compressing; compression resolves into directional moves — position for expansion via straddle-like longs (buy the breakout in either direction).
strategies.indicators: 5-day realized volatility; 20-day realized volatility; 20-day Donchian high/low
strategies.entry: RealizedVol(5) < 0.5 x RealizedVol(20); place a buy stop at the 20-day high and a sell stop at the 20-day low, valid for the NEXT 5 sessions (GTC for 5 sessions, then cancel); first triggered enters; if both trade in the same session take the one nearer the session open, if equidistant skip. Stop fills follow max(open, level) for buys / min(open, level) for sells
strategies.exit: Opposite 10-day extreme or after 5 sessions
strategies.notes: Chan's post is about Hurst/variance scaling, not compression breakouts. RV(5) < 0.5 x RV(20) is frequent (roughly 10-15% of days) so signals cluster inside quiet regimes. Same mechanism as S038/S094/S095 (G-10); the Bollinger squeeze scored worst of all rules on Be The Puck (30/371). Run as the volatility-compression cluster champion candidate with S094 and S095 as variants.
strategies.parameter_variants: order validity {5 sessions primary; 1, 3}; tie-break {nearer to open primary}

strategies.name: Zweig Breadth Thrust
strategies.concept: Martin Zweig's thrust: when the 10-day EMA of NYSE advance ratio (advances / (advances + declines)) rises rapidly from below 0.40 to above 0.615, a new bull phase is starting — buy immediately.
strategies.universe: SPY; breadth built from our own universe (advancers/decliners among liquid_top_N and all listed common stocks), NYSE A/D data are not in the repo
strategies.indicators: 10-day EMA of NYSE advance ratio; threshold pair (0.40 → 0.615)
strategies.entry: 10-day EMA of advance ratio < 0.40 within the last 10 sessions AND crosses above 0.615 today; buy SPY at close of t
strategies.exit: Close < 50-day SMA or new thrust signal refreshes
strategies.frequency: rare (a handful per decade) — combine with other breadth signals
strategies.sources: [GitHub - phuazz/breadth-thrust-etf (a constituent-breadth thrust, NOT the classic NYSE advance/decline Zweig thrust; its author concludes the S&P 500 is the wrong universe and the signal does not generalise)](https://github.com/phuazz/breadth-thrust-etf); Zweig / Morris classic thresholds (StockCharts; not in the cited repo)
strategies.notes: The phuazz repo computes '% of constituents above their 50-day MA crossing from below 50% to above 80% within 20 trading days' from point-in-time iShares holdings and Norgate delisted data; on the S&P 500 (CSP1) its tuned config gives Sharpe +0.59 at the 43rd percentile of the random-entry null; energy and financials Sharpe <= 0.09. The catalog's classic Zweig thresholds are not in `sources`. Zweig thrusts are rare (N ~ 3-5 in 2016+). If kept: build breadth from our own universe, test the classic thresholds on pre-2016 data where available; otherwise drop.
strategies.data_needs: breadth from own universe (D1); pre-2016 NYSE A/D history (external, optional)

strategies.name: Relative Sector Breadth Rotation
strategies.concept: phuazz sleeve A: each sector's breadth (share of constituent stocks above their own short-term trend) minus the cross-sectional mean isolates sectors with unusual internal strength; overweight them.
strategies.universe: sector ETFs on the PIT sector universe table (11 GICS sectors); breadth computed from our own PIT stock universe mapped to sectors
strategies.indicators: per-sector breadth = share of liquid_top_N stocks (SimFin industry code mapped to sector) above their own 50-day SMA; cross-sectional z-score
strategies.entry: Weekly (Friday close, Monday execution), rank sectors by breadth z-score; buy the top half of sectors (7 of 14 in the source; ~5-6 of 11 here), weighted by positive relative share
strategies.exit: Rebalance weekly; positions exit when they leave the top 7
strategies.notes: RESOLVED (was BLOCKED): the source breadth feature needs point-in-time ETF constituent holdings (the US iShares endpoint has been blocked since 2026-05-16; the repo moved to UK UCITS endpoints and Norgate). It is approximated with our own PIT stock universe mapped to sectors via SimFin industry codes; using today's holdings would be look-ahead. strategies.entry: Oversold switch on (RSI(14) < 29.7) -> buy TQQQ REGARDLESS of the 200-SMA (as on the source page), with TQQQ exposure capped at a registered fraction (1.0, 0.5) of the account; otherwise above SMA(200) -> hold QQQ (unlevered); below SMA(200) -> SHY/BIL. The source's overheated (SQQQ) leg and momentum mix (USMV/UGL/ZROZ/IEI) are NOT implemented

With a $5,000 paper account a -70% drawdown is existential: cap exposure.

strategies.name: Cointegrated ETF Pair Z-Score
strategies.concept: The Springer study's method: form ETF pairs (price ratio), test stationarity monthly, compute a rolling z-score, enter at +/-2, exit at the paper's thresholds; re-form pairs when cointegration breaks. The paper's own verdict is modest: short trading windows where cointegration holds limit long-term profitability.
strategies.universe: pre-registered pair list (identify the paper's 30-pair list from its appendix, or fix a list before the first run); ETFs across equities, bonds, commodities, real estate, international
strategies.indicators: Engle-Granger on log prices with an estimated hedge ratio (the paper's ADF is on the price ratio); 12-month rolling mean and std of the spread; z-score
strategies.entry: Pair passes the cointegration test (p < 0.05) on the formation window; |z| > 2 -> short the rich leg / long the cheap leg. Equal-SHARE counts (paper) and dollar-neutral hedge-ratio sizing both registered. Pair selection and trading windows are disjoint: formation on months t-24..t-12, test on t-12..t
strategies.exit: Close shorts when z falls to 0.75 and longs when z rises to -0.5 (Avellaneda & Lee, as in the paper); monthly re-verification closes the pair if cointegration breaks; +/-3 stop is a registered variant; costs on both legs
strategies.frequency: several open pairs at any time; new entries weekly
strategies.notes: Springer (2000-2024, 30 ETF pairs, 12-month formation, monthly ADF on the ratio, rolling z-score) fetched. The SPY/IVV example (cointegrated for 24 years) yielded 'a modest total profit of 1.01% and a Sharpe ratio of 0.28' at z = 2; lowering the threshold raises profit and Sharpe but also volatility and kurtosis. The earlier z = 0 exit and +/-3 stop differed from the paper. Selecting pairs and testing on the same 12 months with 30 pairs x monthly 5% tests produces ~1.5 false positives per month.
strategies.parameter_variants: exits {z 0.75 / -0.5 primary (paper); z = 0 with +/-3 stop}; sizing {equal-share primary (paper); dollar-neutral with hedge ratio}; entry threshold {2.0 primary; lower thresholds}
strategies.data_needs: ETF total-return daily series for the pair list (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: Gold/Silver Ratio Mean Reversion

strategies.entry: Hedge ratio from a rolling regression of log GLD on log SLV (total-return series); spread z-score (60-day) > +2 -> long SLV / short GLD; z < -2 -> reverse
strategies.exit: z crosses 0; stop at ±3

The ratio trends for months (2018-2020 moved ~80 -> 125 -> 65), so +/-3 stops get hit. GLD and SLV are in daily_10years already. Run once with a regression hedge ratio and accept the null.

strategies.name: GDX/GDXJ Miners Spread
strategies.concept: Senior vs junior gold miners (GDX vs GDXJ) share the gold driver but differ in leverage/liquidity; the spread between them mean-reverts as risk appetite in the gold complex normalizes.
strategies.indicators: GDX/GDXJ price ratio; 60-day rolling z-score

strategies.exit: z crosses 0; stop ±3

strategies.name: Stock-vs-Sector Residual Reversal
strategies.concept: For each stock compute its residual 5-day return versus its industry peers (stock return minus beta x peer return); extreme negative residuals revert because nonfundamental, sector-wide or sentiment-driven selling is misattributed to the name. NY Fed SR 513: only the within-industry residual component of reversal is significant and a strategy built on it earns ~3x the risk-adjusted return of the standard sort.
strategies.universe: liquid_top_N US stocks with PIT industry/sector mapping (SimFin industries or SIC) and equal-weight peer returns (sector ETF where available)
strategies.indicators: 5-day residual return (stock - beta x peer return; 60-day beta estimated through t-1); SMA(200) on the stock (on/off)
strategies.entry: Residual 5-day return in the bottom decile AND stock close > SMA200 (registered on/off); buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound); skip-day variant registered
strategies.exit: Time stop: sell after 5 sessions (primary, fixed horizon); or when the 5-day residual > 0 (noisy), max 10 sessions
strategies.sources: [NY Fed Staff Report 513 - Decomposing Short-Term Return Reversal (within-industry residual)](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr513.html); the Springer ETF-pairs paper cited earlier is about ETF pairs, not stock residuals, and is no longer cited
strategies.notes: Best-supported reversal construct. Long-only is a slice of a market-neutral idea, so the beta of a bottom-decile residual basket is not zero: the null is the vol-matched equal-weight universe. Report raw reversal (S027) next to it as the control and exclude/report earnings-window signals (+/-3 sessions, G-12). The market-neutral flavour of the reversal family.
strategies.parameter_variants: exit {5-session time stop primary; residual > 0 with max 10 sessions}; SMA200 filter {on primary, off}; skip {0 days, 1 day}; peers {SimFin industry equal-weight primary; sector ETF}
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + SimFin industry map + earnings flag (DP-EARN)

strategies.name: Chan-Style Statistical Arbitrage Basket
strategies.concept: Chan's mean-reversion work: on the most recent one-year SP1500 data (2008) his Example 3.8 strategy showed Sharpe 4.8 without cost and 3.5 after 10 bps round trip, on data unseen when the book was written. A market-neutral basket of mean-reverting stock positions is the research-scale idea; ONE year of an extreme-volatility regime is not 'enduring profitability'.
strategies.indicators: 90-day mean-reversion score (e.g., Ornstein-Uhlenbeck half-life from daily closes); beta to SPY; position count
strategies.entry: Stage 1 (simple version first): daily cross-sectional reversal, long-short, dollar- and beta-neutral, opening/closing-auction execution. Stage 2 (only then): each week compute each stock's mean-reversion half-life (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck over 90 days), take the fastest 50, long the bottom-quintile residual vs beta-adjusted market and short the top quintile, weights proportional to 1/half-life, dollar- and beta-neutral
strategies.exit: Positions exit when residuals cross 0; weekly rebalance
strategies.sources: [Ernest Chan — The enduring profitability of mean-reversion strategies](http://epchan.blogspot.com/2008/12/enduring-profitability-of-mean.html)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: Chan's post (9 Dec 2008) reports Sharpe 4.8 (no cost) / 3.5 (10 bps) on one year (2008), not '> 5 before costs', and Example 3.8 belongs to the 2008 book (Quantitative Trading), not Algorithmic Trading (2013). Chan's example is a simple long-short reversal portfolio (verify in the 2008 book); the OU half-life / 50-stock weekly basket is the catalog's design. A 50-name dollar-neutral, beta-neutral basket is not implementable at $5,000 (research scale only) and needs borrow (G-09). Chan stresses opening-auction execution. Chan's stated costs: 10 bps round-trip for SP1500 large caps (try 15 bps).
strategies.parameter_variants: stage {simple daily reversal long-short primary; OU half-life version}; cost {10 bps round trip, 15 bps}
strategies.data_needs: daily_10years (D1) + borrow assumptions; research scale only

strategies.name: Turn-of-the-Month Effect (window grid; absorbs S083)
strategies.concept: All excess US equity market return over 1987-2005 (and 1897-2005) concentrated in the 4-day turn-of-the-month window (last trading day + first three); the other 16 days earned nothing on average (SSRN 917884).
strategies.universe: SPY, IWM and RSP (the effect is documented on equal-weight/CRSP indexes); sector ETFs to raise trade count
strategies.indicators: calendar window grid (entry day -2..-1 relative to the last trading day of the month, exit day +2..+5 of the new month); random-window placebo
strategies.entry: Buy SPY at the close of the SECOND-TO-LAST trading day of the month (so the 4-day window includes the last trading day's own return)
strategies.exit: Sell at the close of the 3rd trading day of the new month (4 daily returns: last day + days 1-3)
strategies.sources: [SSRN 917884 — Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=917884)
strategies.notes: FIXED off-by-one: McConnell & Xu (SSRN 917884, FAJ 2008): returns over the interval beginning the last trading day of the month and ending three days later are significantly higher (all excess market return in 1987-2005 and 1897-2005; no higher standard deviation; present in 31 of 35 countries). Buying the close of the LAST trading day and selling the close of day 3 earns only three daily returns; the four-day window needs entry at the close of the second-to-last day (as Be The Puck). Erosion: Trading Garden S&P 500 (MES): 1963-today 765 trades, 58% win, CAGR 11.2% vs 10.9% buy-and-hold, but since 2000 only 321 trades with CAGR 3.0%; Be The Puck beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 63/372. Time in market is ~19%, so judge per unit of exposure against a random-window placebo; report a subperiod table. Absorbs S083 (month-end rebalancing drift: open of the second-to-last trading day to close of the first trading day, 3 sessions; the 'pension rebalancing pushes the index up' story is state-dependent, so report the sign by prior-month return).
strategies.parameter_variants: window {entry close of day -2, exit close of day +3 primary; entry day -2 or -1, exit day +2..+5 grid; ex-S083: entry OPEN of day -2, exit close of day +1}; split by prior-month return sign; placebo {random 4-day windows}
strategies.data_needs: SPY, IWM, RSP total-return daily series (DP-ETF) + trading calendar (DP-CAL)

strategies.name: Pre-Holiday Effect
strategies.concept: The documented anomaly (Lakonishok-Smidt 1988; Ariel 1990) is a high return ON the last trading day before a holiday. The StockCharts page describes the mechanism as traders lightening up before long weekends; the earlier concept text claimed the opposite price pressure and is corrected.
strategies.indicators: exchange holiday calendar
strategies.entry: Buy at the close two sessions before a market holiday (i.e., the close of the second-to-last session before the holiday)
strategies.exit: Sell at the close of the last session before the holiday (primary: captures the documented pre-holiday-day return); alternate: exit the first session after the holiday. Exclude early-close days (July 3, day after Thanksgiving) or report them separately
strategies.notes: ChartSchool describes: purchase equities one or two days before a holiday (selling pressure before a three-day holiday) with results by holiday and an original study of 419 closings 1928-1975; documented sample ends 1975. Holiday count is ~9-10 per year (~90 events in 2016+; Juneteenth since 2022). Be The Puck: beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 91/372. Volume is very light on pre-holiday sessions: use conservative fills.
strategies.parameter_variants: exit {close of last session before holiday primary; first session after holiday}; early-close days {excluded primary; separate}
strategies.data_needs: SPY total-return daily series (DP-ETF) + exchange holiday calendar (DP-CAL)

strategies.name: Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
strategies.concept: Lucca-Moench (JF 2015; NY Fed SR 512): SPX rose 49 bp on average in the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC announcements (Sept 1994 - Mar 2011), about 80% of annual realized excess stock returns, with a holding-only-those-windows strategy at an annualised Sharpe of 1.1 or higher. Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert (FRL 2021): the drift 'essentially disappeared after 2015'.
strategies.indicators: FOMC meeting calendar (scheduled announcements)
strategies.entry: Buy SPY at the close of the session BEFORE the scheduled announcement day t (announcement at 14:00 ET on day t; use federalreserve.gov dates; the announcement day is the second day of two-day meetings; exclude unscheduled meetings)
strategies.exit: Primary: sell at the OPEN of announcement day t (strictly pre-announcement). Alternates: close of day t (includes the 2 pm reaction); with SPY minute bars (2023-09+): 14:00(t-1) to 14:00(t), the faithful window
strategies.notes: FIXED: the window is ~14:00 on the day before to ~14:00 on the announcement day; the earlier 'sell at the open AFTER the announcement' held through the 2 pm release and the following night, contradicting its own 'exit before reaction risk' justification. The '>30x other days' figure is not in the abstract or introduction (which say 'orders of magnitude larger') and is removed. Expect near zero post-2015: split subperiods at 2015. Placebo = the same windows before other macro announcements. Be The Puck: beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 43/372 ('kept to show that'). Eight scheduled meetings a year; pair with S079/S080 in one calendar basket.
strategies.parameter_variants: exit {open of announcement day primary; close of announcement day; 14:00 to 14:00 minute version}; subperiods {to 2015, after 2015}; placebo {other macro announcements}
strategies.data_needs: SPY daily bars (DP-ETF); SPY minute bars 2023-09+; FOMC calendar (DP-CAL)

strategies.name: Options-Expiration-Week Drift
strategies.concept: Monthly options expiration (3rd Friday) forces gamma-driven flows into the cash market in expiration week; pinning and post-expiration drift are documented market-microstructure effects.
strategies.indicators: monthly options expiration calendar (3rd Friday); week-of-month counter
strategies.entry: Buy SPY at the close of the session before expiration week begins (typically the 2nd Thursday/Friday of the month)
strategies.exit: Sell at the close of the Monday after expiration (post-expiration drift)
strategies.hold: ~6 sessions (entry the session before expiration week to the close of the Monday after expiration)
strategies.notes: Placebo test only. The window is ~6 sessions, not the earlier '3-5'. Option-expiry literature concerns pinning and volatility effects, not drift; the Atlas (11.4) treats expiry as a calendar FEATURE to avoid mistaking settlement mechanics for information; daily/0DTE SPX options since 2022 weaken any monthly-gamma narrative. Use expiry-week dummies as a control variable in S079/S081 studies; run the simple drift once as a placebo test, otherwise drop. The cited page is an index (no rule).
strategies.data_needs: SPY total-return daily series (DP-ETF) + options-expiry calendar (DP-CAL)

strategies.name: 20-Day-EMA Pullback in Uptrend
strategies.concept: A liquid stock in a long-term uptrend (above 200-day SMA) that pulls back to its 20-day EMA is at the institutional buy zone; entries at the EMA get trend exposure at discount prices.
strategies.entry: Close(t) > SMA200 AND low(t) <= EMA20(t) (touch or cross below) AND a pullback-depth condition (3-day return <= -x%, registered x in {2, 3, 5}, or rank by distance below the EMA); buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound). Report signal frequency per 500 stocks before sizing
strategies.exit: Close > 10-day SMA; sell at close of that session; stop: close < EMA(20) - 2 x ATR(14); max 8 sessions (stop sits ~2 ATR below entry vs a 10-day SMA reclaim exit: the risk/reward is skewed against the trade, report it)
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.notes: The old condition repeated close > SMA200 twice. In stocks above the 200-day SMA the low touches EMA(20) on a large fraction of days, so 'several per week' signals are unselective: the pullback-depth condition or distance ranking is added. The 20-EMA pullback is standard swing practice; Connors' family uses shallower pullbacks (5-day MA exits), see S001. Report with and without earnings-window signals (+/-3 sessions, G-12).
strategies.parameter_variants: pullback depth x {none, 2%, 3%, 5%}; earnings window {included, excluded}

strategies.name: MACD Bullish Cross with Volume
strategies.concept: MACD(12,26,9) crossing above zero after a pullback marks momentum re-acceleration; volume confirmation separates genuine re-acceleration from dead-cat bounces.
strategies.indicators: MACD(12,26,9); 20-day median volume; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: MACD line crosses above signal line AND MACD > 0 AND close > SMA200 AND volume(t) > 1.3 × 20-day median; buy at open of t+1
strategies.exit: MACD crosses below signal line; sell at close of that session; max 10 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.notes: Rule-zoo audit member, not an independent strategy. Atlas 10.6 (Rink 2023; Chuang 2024; Yang 2020b): MACD/MA-type rules show no out-of-sample persistence after data-snooping correction; Be The Puck MACD Signal Cross beats buy-and-hold Sharpe on 59/372. 'MACD > 0 AND signal cross' is a late signal and 1.3x median volume is arbitrary; hold the parameterization fixed and report sensitivity. Include in the rule-zoo audit (G-05).

strategies.name: Golden Cross with Slope Filter
strategies.concept: The 50/200 golden cross is the classic regime signal; requiring a rising 200-day SMA slope filters out crosses in sideways markets (whipsaw source).
strategies.indicators: SMA(50); SMA(200); SMA(200) 20-day slope
strategies.entry: SMA50 crosses above SMA200 AND SMA200(t) > SMA200(t-20); buy at close of t
strategies.exit: SMA50 crosses below SMA200; sell at close of that session
strategies.frequency: rare per instrument (~1 per 2 years); run across 20+ instruments for a live pipeline
strategies.notes: Use as a regime OVERLAY (long-only gate on/off) in the champions' test rather than a standalone strategy. Trading Garden golden cross (S&P): 33 trades 1963-today, 78.8% win, CAGR 11.8%, max drawdown 19.9%/25.5% (best risk profile in its table) but only 13 trades since 2000 (~4-5 SPY events in 2016+); Be The Puck beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 106/371 (best of the trend rules). The slope filter is a second parameter. As a standalone it has too few events; as a regime gate it is credible.

strategies.name: KAMA Breakout
strategies.concept: Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) tightens in sideways markets and loosens in trends; price crossing KAMA after a quiet period is an adaptive breakout signal that self-tunes to volatility.
strategies.indicators: KAMA(10, 2, 30); 20-day realized volatility
strategies.entry: Close(t) > KAMA(t) AND KAMA flat-to-rising (KAMA(t) > KAMA(t-5) × 0.999); buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close < KAMA; sell at close of that session
strategies.notes: Run once with the standard KAMA(10,2,30) formula and accept the null. The only source is a YouTube marketing claim ($124k on NQ; page empty in review); Be The Puck's Kaufman Adaptive MA beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 44/372; `KAMA(t) > KAMA(t-5) x 0.999` is an arbitrary slope test.

strategies.name: Donchian 55 with Chandelier Trail
strategies.concept: Turtle System 2 entries (55-day breakout) with a 3×ATR(22) chandelier trailing stop from the highest high since entry — the trailing exit lets winners run far beyond the channel exit.
strategies.indicators: 55-day Donchian high/low; ATR(22); chandelier stop (highest high − 3 × ATR)
strategies.entry: Close(t) > 55-day high; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close < highest high since entry − 3 × ATR(22); mirror for shorts
strategies.frequency: 1-3 trades per year per instrument across 10-20 ETFs
strategies.notes: Exit variant of the Donchian family (S036, speed 55): the 3 x ATR(22) chandelier is ~6-9% below the high for equities, tight relative to the volatility of 55-day swings, and induces churn; Be The Puck's Chandelier Exit beat buy-and-hold on 74/372. Run as `S036 --speed 55 --exit chandelier` and compare with the 20-day-low and 2N exits. Kagels has no chandelier rule (catalog's own).

strategies.name: Higher-Low Reversal Entry
strategies.concept: After a decline, two consecutive sessions with higher lows signal sellers are exhausted; volume confirmation marks accumulation (Wyckoff-style daily-bar pattern). As originally written the rule selected an ongoing rise, so a prior-decline precondition is now explicit.
strategies.indicators: 2-day higher-low sequence; prior-decline condition; volume vs 20-day median; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Prior decline (definition A: 5-10 day drawdown >= x% from the recent high; definition B: RSI(5) < 40 within the last 5 sessions; both registered) AND close(t) > SMA200 AND low(t) > low(t-1) > low(t-2) AND volume(t) > 1.2 x 20-day median AND close(t) > open(t); buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close < low(t-1) (structure broken) or close > 10-day SMA; max 8 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.notes: Pattern definitions are unambiguous on daily bars. Without a decline precondition the original entry (above SMA200, rising lows, bullish bar, volume) is a continuation entry, not a reversal; report both decline definitions and the version without any precondition as the control. Report with and without earnings-window signals (G-12).
strategies.parameter_variants: decline definition {A: drawdown >= x%, B: RSI(5) < 40}; control {no precondition}

strategies.name: Bollinger Squeeze Breakout
strategies.concept: When Bollinger Band width (20-day, 2 sd) falls to a 6-month low, volatility is compressed; the squeeze resolves directionally — trade the first close outside the bands.
strategies.indicators: Bollinger Bands (20-day, 2 sd); band width percentile (120-day)
strategies.entry: Band width in bottom decile of last 120 sessions AND close(t) > upper band; buy at close of t (mirror for lower band)
strategies.exit: Close crosses the 20-day middle band against the position; max 10 sessions
strategies.notes: Compression cluster member (variant of S065), executed via band-close rather than stop orders. The Be The Puck squeeze rule (BandWidth at its lowest of 125 days, close above the upper band, exit below the 20-day average) beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on only 30/371, the worst of its breakout family. The unused '20-day Donchian confirmation' indicator is removed from the list.

strategies.name: Keltner Channel Breakout
strategies.concept: Keltner Channels (20-day EMA ± 2 × ATR(10)) are trend-following bands; a close above the upper channel marks trend initiation with volatility-based (not standard-deviation-based) bands.
strategies.indicators: Keltner Channel (EMA(20), ATR(10), multiplier 2); 20-day median volume
strategies.entry: Close(t) > upper Keltner band AND volume > 1.3 × 20-day median; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close < middle band (EMA20); sell at close of that session; max 10 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per month across a universe
strategies.notes: Compression/channel cluster member only (correlated with S094). Be The Puck's Keltner rule (EMA20 + 2 x ATR10; exit below the EMA) beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 46/372 and returned +2.1%/yr on the S&P 500 index vs +8.9%; the cited TradingView page is a script listing, not a source. Report the correlation with S094.

strategies.name: Three-Bar Reversal (Bulkowski)
strategies.concept: Bulkowski's three-bar reversal as defined on the cited TradingView (HPotter) page: daily bars; the middle day has the lowest low of the three days (no ties); the last day closes above the prior day's high (no ties); each day has a nonzero trading range. A short-term reversal signature.
strategies.indicators: 3-bar pattern per the source definition; SMA(200) (catalog addition)
strategies.entry: Pattern completes: low(t-1) < low(t-2) AND low(t-1) < low(t) AND close(t) > high(t-1), no ties, high != low on each of the three bars; buy at close of bar 3 (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound). Registered variant: AND close > SMA200 (catalog addition)
strategies.exit: Close < pattern low (the middle bar's low) or after 5 sessions; sell at close (the exit is the catalog's addition, registered)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: the earlier 'bar 2 range inside bar 1's range, bar 3 close above bar 1's close' was a different pattern and 'inside' contradicted 'lowest low of the three'. The SMA200 gate and the 5-session/pattern-low exit are the catalog's additions. Compare against random bars of equal frequency; register pattern, length, distance threshold and holding rule before testing (Atlas pattern registry). Based on Bulkowski's Stocks & Commodities article (Jan 2000).
strategies.parameter_variants: gate {none primary; SMA200}; exit {pattern low / 5 sessions primary}; mirror short {long-only first}

strategies.name: Bullish Engulfing After Down-Streak
strategies.concept: A bullish engulfing candle (session body engulfs the prior bearish body) after 3+ down closes marks capitulation followed by aggressive buying — conditioned on the streak to avoid random engulfing noise.
strategies.indicators: engulfing pattern test; 3-day down-close streak; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: 3+ consecutive down closes (close(t-1) < open(t-1) bearish prior bar), then session t with close(t) > open(t) AND open(t) < close(t-1) AND close(t) > open(t-1) (current body fully engulfs prior body) AND close(t) > SMA200; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close > 5-day SMA or first up-close target; max 5 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per week across the universe
strategies.notes: Candlestick registry member (S096-S100), tested under a family-wise (FDR) correction; compare with S030 (streak) without the pattern ('the desk question is always whether the pattern label adds information beyond the raw window'). Be The Puck's engulfing switch beat buy-and-hold Sharpe on 45/372 and returned +4.4%/yr on the S&P 500 index vs +8.9%. The 3-down-closes-then-engulf condition is mostly S030/S007 with a candlestick overlay. The strict engulfing definition is primary; test the loose variant (close above prior close, open below prior open).

strategies.name: Hammer at Lower Bollinger Band
strategies.concept: A hammer (long lower wick, small body near the session high) at the lower Bollinger Band is a rejection of extreme prices — buyers defended the lower extreme within the session.
strategies.indicators: hammer defined on the range (lower wick >= 60% of the high-low range AND close in the top third of the range, no zero-body failure); Bollinger Band (20-day, 2 sd); SMA(200)
strategies.entry: Hammer (range-based definition) forms AND low(t) < lower Bollinger band AND close(t) > SMA200; buy at close of t (fill: moc_proxy primary; next_open alternate; close fill only as an upper bound)
strategies.exit: Close > 20-day middle band; max 5 sessions
strategies.notes: The earlier definition (lower wick > 2 x body AND upper wick < body) is unsatisfiable for doji bars (body = 0) and noisy for tiny bodies; the range-based definition replaces it. `low(t) < lower band` (an intraday touch) differs from S011's close below the band, and this is the same cluster as S011. Candlestick registry member.

strategies.name: Outside-Day Key Reversal at 200-SMA
strategies.concept: An outside day (higher high, lower low) that closes green against a prior down-close, landing on the 200-day SMA, is a battle won by buyers at the most-watched level in the market.
strategies.indicators: outside-day test; prior down-close; SMA(200)
strategies.entry: high(t) > high(t-1) AND low(t) < low(t-1) AND close(t) > open(t) AND close(t-1) < open(t-1) AND |close(t) − SMA200| / close(t) < 1%; buy at close of t
strategies.exit: Close < low(t) (reversal low broken) or close > 10-day SMA; max 8 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per month across a universe
strategies.notes: Candlestick registry member. Classical key reversal is a new low followed by a close above the prior close; this outside-day variant plus 'within 1% of SMA200' is rare and arbitrary. Measure the signal frequency first (the earlier 'several per month across a universe' is unverified) and drop if there are fewer than 100 events in the dev period. 200-SMA proximity is a free parameter.

strategies.name: Three White Soldiers Continuation
strategies.concept: Three consecutive long green candles each closing above the prior close signals sustained aggressive buying; in an established uptrend it predicts continuation, not exhaustion.
strategies.indicators: 3-session pattern (each close > prior close, each close > open, each open within prior body); SMA(50); volume trend
strategies.entry: Pattern completes AND close > SMA50 AND volume rising across the 3 sessions; buy at close of the third session
strategies.exit: First close below the pattern's first session low; max 8 sessions
strategies.frequency: several per month across a universe
strategies.notes: Falsification against S027's sign: three strong up days put the stock in the top of its 3-day return distribution, the state where the short-term reversal literature (S027, NY Fed SR 513) expects give-back, and S100 bets on continuation without a reason to expect it to win. It is the mirror of S030/S031 logic. Register as a falsification test; candlestick registry member.

strategies.name: Copper/Gold Ratio Equity Tilt (CPER/GLD ratio, both in cache)
strategies.concept: The copper/gold ratio is a real-time growth-vs-fear indicator (copper = industrial demand, gold = fear hedge); a rising ratio favors cyclical stocks, a falling ratio favors defensives — rotating between them monetizes the macro signal.
strategies.universe: XLB/XLI (cyclicals) vs XLP/XLU (defensives); signal ratio CPER/GLD (both in daily_10years, 2016+)
strategies.indicators: CPER/GLD price ratio; 63-day z-score of the ratio
strategies.entry: Each week, if the CPER/GLD 21-day change > 0 AND 63-day z > 0, hold the cyclical basket; else hold the defensive basket. Registered control: plain relative momentum of (XLB+XLI) minus (XLP+XLU) with no copper input
strategies.exit: Weekly re-evaluation; switch on signal flip
strategies.sources: [PortfoliosLab - Momentum & sector rotation (generic; does not describe a copper/gold idea)](https://portfolioslab.com/strategies/momentum-rotation)
strategies.notes: RESOLVED (was BLOCKED): CPER launched in late 2011 and is already in the daily_10years cache from 2016-01-04 (2,718 rows; thinly traded with zero-volume days: apply the data-hygiene mask), as are GLD and USO, so the CPER/GLD ratio is testable on 2016+ without futures data; no pre-2016 regime coverage is claimed. The ratio's relationship to cyclicals vs defensives flips with the rate regime and `21-day change > 0 AND 63-day z > 0` flips often, so test against the simple relative-momentum control and accept the null if it adds nothing. Sector ETFs XLB/XLI/XLP/XLU need DP-ETF.
strategies.parameter_variants: signal {CPER/GLD ratio primary; relative momentum of cyclical minus defensive baskets (no copper)}; cadence {weekly primary; monthly}
strategies.data_needs: CPER and GLD in daily_10years (D1); XLB, XLI, XLP, XLU (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: Yield-Curve Financials/Utilities Rotation
strategies.concept: A steepening yield curve (10Y−2Y slope rising) compresses bank net-interest margins favorably and hurts utilities (bond proxies); a flattening curve reverses it. Rotating between XLF and XLU on curve-momentum harvests rate-regime flows.
strategies.indicators: 10Y yield level change and 2Y yield change (separately); optional 10Y-2Y slope
strategies.entry: Monthly decision (dead band): use the 21-day change in the 10Y yield and in the 2Y yield separately (bull steepening via falling short rates vs bear steepening via rising long rates have opposite implications for utilities); hold XLF when the signal favours steepening by bank NIM logic beyond the dead band, else XLU
strategies.exit: Weekly re-evaluation
strategies.notes: The 21-day change in the 10Y-2Y slope switches sign about weekly in a flat curve, and the mechanism is ambiguous (bull vs bear steepening). Only 2016-2026 episodes (2019 inversion, 2022-23 inversion) give independent regimes. Accept the null if not significant after FDR. The PortfoliosLab citation does not describe curve rotation.
strategies.parameter_variants: decision cadence {monthly with dead band primary; weekly}; signal {10Y and 2Y changes separately primary; slope change}
strategies.data_needs: FRED T10Y2Y, DGS10, DGS2 (DP-FRED); XLF, XLU (DP-ETF)

strategies.name: High-Beta/Momentum Crash Protection (overlay comparison on S041)
strategies.concept: Momentum crashes after market declines (Chan: after a crisis momentum strategies get hurt in the rebound; one remedy is to stop shorting after a market fall and trade only the long side post-crisis; his preferred approach is running momentum and mean reversion together). The evidenced mitigation is scaling momentum by its own trailing realised volatility (Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015: it 'nearly doubles the Sharpe ratio while virtually eliminating crashes'). This entry compares three overlays on S041.
strategies.indicators: market drawdown from 252-day high; strategy's own 126-day realised volatility; momentum decile rank
strategies.entry: Hold the S041 top-decile 12-1 portfolio under three registered overlays, compared out of sample: (a) catalog gate: hold while SPY is within 10% of its 252-day high; (b) vol-scaling: exposure w_t = sigma_target / sigma_hat_t with sigma_hat = realised daily vol of the strategy's own return over the previous 126 days annualised, sigma_target = 12% (long-short) or the unscaled strategy's full-sample vol (long-only), capped at 1.0 (optionally 1.5-2.0), re-sized monthly; (c) none
strategies.exit: (a) move to cash when SPY falls more than 10% below its 252-day high, re-enter on a new 63-day high (late both ways); (b) monthly re-scaling; (c) none
strategies.sources: [Better System Trader - Ernie Chan (momentum-crash discussion)](https://bettersystemtrader.com/012-ernest-chan/); Barroso & Santa-Clara (2015) (Atlas 9.6, 18.4, 18.6)
strategies.notes: CORRECTED: Chan advises stopping SHORTS after a crisis; a long-only de-risk-to-cash gate is not Chan's advice, and the 10%-from-high trigger with 'new 63-day high' re-entry is a drawdown gate that is late both ways. Test crash months (Apr-May 2020 analogue) and overlay turnover; the Atlas's honest benchmark asks whether a change-point gate beats plain vol scaling.
strategies.parameter_variants: overlay {(a) catalog gate; (b) vol-scaling primary candidate; (c) none}; vol target {12% L/S; unscaled full-sample vol long-only}; cap {1.0 primary; 1.5-2.0}

strategies.name: Volatility-Targeted Overnight Carry
strategies.concept: Combine the overnight premium (S021) with volatility scaling: hold the overnight session sized inversely to current volatility — more exposure in calm markets, less in stressed ones (Barroso/Santa-Clara vol-scaling improves Sharpe for momentum strategies; applied here to the overnight premium).
strategies.indicators: 20-day realized volatility of the OVERNIGHT (close-to-open) return series, dividend-correct; target 10% annualized; overnight holding schedule
strategies.entry: Each day, size overnight SPY exposure = 10% / (annualized realized vol of the overnight return series, 20 days), capped at 1x (the $5,000 unlevered account) and, separately, 2x (needs margin); buy at close; re-size only when the target exposure moves outside a 20% band
strategies.exit: Sell at open; re-size daily
strategies.sources: [SSRN — Night Trading (overnight premium)](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=2633476); Attached paper (user upload) — Borsa Istanbul (volatility scaling, Barroso & Santa-Clara)] — attached PDF (user upload), no public URL verified
strategies.notes: Sizing vol must come from the overnight return series (what is actually held), not close-to-close vol, otherwise the 10% target is misdefined (overnight vol is a fraction of total vol). The null is S021 unscaled on identical dividend-correct data: the question is whether scaling improves Sharpe/drawdown, not whether the premium exists; Barroso-Santa-Clara scaling is documented for momentum, not for the overnight premium. The attached Borsa paper credits breadth (equal-weighting, p = 0.034 vs cap-weighted) plus risk scaling for its whole improvement, not volatility scaling alone. Report turnover of the resizing and costs per the S021 ladder. The Efficiente 5 paper is not a source for this entry.
strategies.parameter_variants: leverage cap {1x primary; 2x}; resizing {20% band primary; daily}; vol window {20-day overnight primary}
